title: Forgot my password
body: Symptoms: You type your password at the sign-in screen and it is rejected, or you cannot remember which password you set. Cause: Passwords are easy to forget, especially after a long break or a recent change. Steps: 1. Click the 'Forgot password' link on the sign-in page. 2. Enter your work email address exactly as it appears in the staff directory. 3. Open the reset email from the IT self-service portal. It usually arrives within five minutes; check your spam folder too. 4. Click the link within 30 minutes, because it expires. 5. Create a new password of at least 14 characters that you have not used before. 6. Sign in with the new password on your laptop and phone. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk by phone or the help chat and ask for a password reset. Give your employee number so the team can verify you.

title: Account locked after failed attempts
body: Symptoms: The sign-in screen says your account is locked, or the sign-in button is greyed out. Cause: Too many wrong password attempts trigger an automatic security lock, usually for 15 minutes or until IT unlocks it. Steps: 1. Stop trying the password, because each failed attempt can extend the lock. 2. Wait 15 minutes before doing anything else. 3. Check whether an old phone, tablet or email app is quietly retrying an outdated password. 4. Close those apps or sign out of them. 5. After the wait, try signing in once with the correct password. 6. If the lock remains, use the 'Unlock account' option on the self-service portal, or ask the help desk to unlock it. Still stuck? Call the IT help desk from your desk phone. Do not share your password with a colleague to try for you.

title: Password has expired
body: Symptoms: After entering your password, a message says it has expired and must be changed before you can sign in. Cause: Company policy requires a new password every 180 days, and the reminder period has passed. Steps: 1. Sign in with your current password when the expired message appears. 2. Follow the prompt to create a new password. 3. Use at least 14 characters, mixing words that are easy for you to remember but hard for others to guess. 4. Do not reuse any of your last five passwords. 5. Confirm the new password when asked. 6. Update the password on your phone and laptop email settings so they do not keep using the old one. Still stuck? If the change page will not load, use a different browser or contact the help desk for assistance.

title: Verification code not arriving
body: Symptoms: You are asked for a verification code after your password, but no code appears on your phone or the code is rejected. Cause: Notifications for the authenticator app may be turned off, the phone may have no signal, or the phone's clock may be wrong so codes do not match. Steps: 1. Open the authenticator app and check that it shows a code for your work account. 2. Make sure the phone has mobile data or Wi-Fi turned on. 3. Turn on notifications for the authenticator app in your phone settings. 4. Set your phone to automatic date and time so its clock is accurate. 5. Wait for a new code, because codes change every 30 seconds, and enter the latest one. 6. Try the 'Resend code' or 'Use another method' option on the sign-in page. Still stuck? Contact the help desk and ask for a temporary code.

title: New phone and the authenticator app
body: Symptoms: You replaced or reset your phone and can no longer get codes for your work sign-in. Cause: The authenticator app is linked to the old phone, so its codes do not work on a new device. Steps: 1. Do not restore the old phone's backup onto the new phone without checking first. 2. On a computer, sign in to the IT self-service portal and choose 'Manage sign-in methods'. 3. Remove the old phone from your list of methods. 4. Install the authenticator app on the new phone and add your work account again. 5. Confirm the setup by entering a code shown on the new phone. 6. Keep a backup code printed or stored safely in a locked drawer. Still stuck? Your identity must be verified before the old method can be removed, so contact the help desk in person or by phone.

title: Sign-in keeps asking for password
body: Symptoms: The sign-in page keeps reappearing after you enter your password, or you are asked to sign in again every few minutes. Cause: Old browser cookies, saved sign-in details or a stuck browser session are blocking the sign-in from completing. Steps: 1. Save any open work first. 2. Close all windows of the browser you use for work. 3. Open the browser's settings and clear browsing data for the last 24 hours, including cookies and cached files. Do not clear saved passwords. 4. Restart the browser and go to the company intranet page. 5. Sign in once more and watch for the confirmation message. 6. If it still loops, try a different browser that the company approves. Still stuck? Note the exact message on screen, take a photo of it with your phone, and send it to the help desk so they can see the error.

title: Correct password rejected by Caps Lock or keyboard
body: Symptoms: You are sure the password is right, but the sign-in screen rejects it. Some letters or symbols appear different from what you expected. Cause: Caps Lock may be on, or the keyboard may be set to another language, which changes the symbols you type. Steps: 1. Look for the Caps Lock light on your keyboard and turn it off if it is lit. 2. Check the language indicator in the taskbar at the bottom of your screen. If it shows another language, switch to English using the taskbar. 3. Type the password slowly in a plain text editor first to see the characters clearly. 4. Be careful with the number zero and the letter O, and with the number one and the letter l. 5. Try typing the password again in the sign-in box. 6. If you use the on-screen keyboard, check that it is set to the same language. Still stuck? Contact the help desk. They can check whether the account is locked or the password needs a reset.

title: Password manager will not fill in
body: Symptoms: The password manager does not offer to fill in your work password, or the saved password fails when used. Cause: The saved entry is out of date after a password change, or the password manager is not connected to the sign-in page address. Steps: 1. Open the password manager and search for the work sign-in entry. 2. Check that the website address in the entry matches the company sign-in page exactly. 3. If the password is old, update it by signing in manually and choosing to save the new password. 4. Delete any duplicate entries for the same account so the wrong one is not used. 5. Lock the password manager and unlock it again to refresh the list. 6. Only use the password manager that the company has approved, and never store the password in a plain document. Still stuck? Contact the help desk and describe which website address the manager suggests.

title: Old password still saved on devices
body: Symptoms: Your email or chat app on a phone or tablet keeps showing an error or asking you to sign in, even though you can sign in on your laptop. Cause: After a password change, devices and apps still use the old saved password and keep retrying it, which can lock your account. Steps: 1. Start with your phone, because it is the most common device with an old password. 2. Open your email app settings and find the work account. 3. Remove the account or choose to sign in again, then enter the new password. 4. Repeat on the chat app, the calendar app and any tablet you use for work. 5. On your laptop, sign out of the company VPN app and sign back in with the new password. 6. Wait a few minutes and check that no more error messages appear. Still stuck? If an app still fails, contact the help desk and tell them which devices you have changed.

title: New password not accepted
body: Symptoms: When you choose a new password, the change page shows a message saying it does not meet the requirements, or it will not save. Cause: The password is too short, has been used recently, contains your name or is missing a required type of character. Steps: 1. Read the requirements shown above the password box before you type. 2. Make the password at least 14 characters long. 3. Include a mix of uppercase, lowercase and numbers, as the page requires. 4. Avoid your name, your username, the company name and simple patterns like Summer2024. 5. Do not reuse any of your last five passwords. 6. Type the new password in both boxes and click Save again. Still stuck? Copy the exact message shown on the screen and send it to the help desk so they can check the policy settings with you.

title: Reset link email lands in spam
body: Symptoms: You request a password reset link from the sign-in page, but the email never shows up in your inbox. The page may say the email was sent, yet nothing arrives after several minutes. Cause: Reset emails are often filtered into the junk or spam folder, or a mail rule treats messages from the sign-in system as unknown senders. Steps: 1. Check your junk, spam and promotions folders. 2. Search your mailbox for the words reset or password. 3. If you find the message, select Not spam and open the link within 30 minutes, since reset links expire. 4. If nothing is there, wait five minutes and request a new link only once, because repeated requests can confuse the reset process. 5. Ask the help desk to confirm the email address on your account is correct and matches the one you use every day. Still stuck? Contact the help desk by phone or the chat app. Include the time you sent the request and the email address you used, but never include your password in your message.

title: Authenticator code times out before I can enter it
body: Symptoms: The six-digit code in the authenticator app disappears or expires while you are typing, and the sign-in page rejects it with a message saying the code is invalid. Cause: Codes change every 30 seconds. If you start typing near the end of a cycle, the code can expire before you finish. Your phone clock may also be a few minutes off from the real time, which makes codes look wrong. Steps: 1. Open the authenticator app and wait until the countdown circle is nearly full, which means a new code has just started. 2. Type the new code quickly and submit it straight away. 3. If it still fails, open your phone settings and turn on automatic date and time. 4. Close the authenticator app fully, reopen it, and try again with the newest code. 5. Make sure you are using the code for the right account, since several accounts can appear in the app. Still stuck? Ask the help desk for a one-time backup code, and mention whether your phone clock was set manually.

title: Locked out after changing my password on another device
body: Symptoms: You changed your password on your laptop, but your phone email app or the chat app keeps failing and then asks you to sign in again. Your account may show a temporary lock after several failed attempts. Cause: Apps on your phone and tablet still send the old password in the background. Each failed try counts toward the lock limit, so the account locks quickly. Steps: 1. Stop trying to sign in on the old devices right away. 2. Wait 15 minutes so the temporary lock can clear. 3. On your phone, open your email app settings and remove the saved account. 4. Add the account again and type your new password carefully. 5. Repeat the same steps for the chat app and any tablet you use. 6. Sign in to the company portal on your laptop to confirm everything works. Still stuck? Contact the help desk and list which devices you updated, so staff can check the lock status without guessing.

title: Password change page shows a blank screen
body: Symptoms: When you open the change password page, the form area stays white with no boxes or buttons, even after waiting a minute. Cause: The page is often blocked by an old browser, a browser extension that hides page content, or a saved session that has timed out. Steps: 1. Close the tab completely and open the change password page again from the sign-in page. 2. Try a private or incognito window, which runs without extensions. 3. Turn off browser extensions such as ad blockers, then reload the page. 4. Update your browser to the latest version using its settings menu, then restart it. 5. Clear the saved site data for the sign-in page only, then sign in again. 6. If you are on a phone, try your laptop instead, since some phone browsers display this page poorly. Still stuck? Send the help desk a screenshot of the full browser window, the browser name and version, and the time you tried. Never type your current or new password into any message.

title: Sign-in page keeps redirecting in a loop
body: Symptoms: After you enter your username and password, the page reloads and sends you back to the sign-in page again. This may repeat several times before you see an error message. Cause: Browser cookies that remember your session may be blocked, outdated, or conflicting with another login you have open. Steps: 1. Open browser settings and make sure cookies are allowed for the sign-in site. 2. Close every window of the browser, then open a new one. 3. Sign out of any other company websites you have open in other tabs. 4. Clear cookies for the sign-in site only, not all browser data. 5. Sign in again in a private window to test whether the loop stops. 6. If the loop continues, try a different browser on the same laptop and note which one works. Still stuck? Contact the help desk and mention which browser you use and whether you recently changed any browser settings or security tools.

title: Single sign-on button missing from the sign-in page
body: Symptoms: The sign-in page shows only the username and password boxes, but you expected a button for signing in with your company account. The page may look different from what a colleague sees. Cause: The sign-in option can be hidden if you typed a personal email address, if your account uses a different sign-in method, or if you are on an old web address. Steps: 1. Type your full work email address in the username box, not a short name. 2. Wait a few seconds after typing, because the page may update to show the sign-in option. 3. If the button still does not appear, refresh the page once. 4. Check that the web address matches the company portal address your team uses, and bookmark it. 5. Ask your manager whether your account was recently moved to a different sign-in method. Still stuck? Contact the help desk with your work email address and the exact web address you used, so staff can check your account setup.

title: Security question answers keep being rejected
body: Symptoms: When you answer your security question, the page says the answer is wrong, even though you are sure it is right. You may have answered it correctly months ago. Cause: Answers are often case sensitive, and spacing and punctuation can count. You may be typing a different spelling or format from the one you originally set up. Steps: 1. Check that Caps Lock is off and that your keyboard layout is correct before typing. 2. Type the answer exactly as you first set it, including capital letters, spaces and punctuation. 3. Do not guess repeatedly, because several wrong answers can lock the account. 4. If you are unsure, wait until later and try once more with a fresh mind. 5. If you cannot recall the answer, ask the help desk to verify your identity another way. Still stuck? Contact the help desk by phone or in person. Do not share your answer in chat or email, because staff will ask you questions to confirm who you are.

title: Trusted device prompt appears every time I sign in
body: Symptoms: Each time you sign in on your laptop, the sign-in page asks you to confirm the device again, even though you chose to remember it last time. The prompt can appear several times in a single day. Cause: Your browser may delete cookies when it closes, or the trusted device setting may expire after a set number of days. Private windows also forget trusted devices by design. Steps: 1. When the prompt appears, tick the box that says to trust this device. 2. Confirm the request using the authenticator app on your phone. 3. Open browser settings and allow cookies to stay after closing for the sign-in site. 4. Avoid using private windows for daily sign-in. 5. When you sign out, avoid clearing all browser data. 6. Keep a short note of how often the prompt appears, so you can describe the pattern to staff. Still stuck? Contact the help desk and say which browser and laptop you use, plus whether the prompt appears on every site or only the sign-in page.

title: Two-step prompt after changing my email address
body: Symptoms: After your email address changed, the sign-in page asks you to verify a code sent to your old address, or the code never arrives at all. You may be unsure which address the system is using. Cause: Verification methods are tied to the address stored on your account. The old address may still be the recovery route, even though you no longer check that mailbox. Steps: 1. Check whether you can still access the old mailbox from your phone or laptop. 2. If you can, use it to receive the code and sign in. 3. Once signed in, open the account security settings and confirm your new email address is listed. 4. Remove old recovery addresses you no longer use, so codes go to the right place. 5. If you no longer have access to the old mailbox, call the help desk instead of guessing. Still stuck? Contact the help desk with your old and new email addresses and your manager's name, so staff can confirm your identity before making changes.

title: Password manager saves duplicate entries
body: Symptoms: The password manager shows two or three saved entries for the same sign-in page, and the one it fills in automatically may not work. You may be unsure which entry is current. Cause: Entries were created at different times, sometimes with different web addresses or with old passwords that were never removed after a change. Steps: 1. Open the password manager and search for the name of the sign-in site. 2. Compare the web addresses and the last-changed dates on each entry. 3. Sign in with the newest password you know works, and confirm you reach the portal. 4. Once confirmed, delete the old or duplicate entries, checking each one first. 5. Edit the remaining entry to make sure the username and web address are correct. 6. Lock the password manager, reopen it, and test that it fills in correctly. Still stuck? Contact the help desk and tell them which password manager you use. Do not send screenshots that show any passwords.

title: Authenticator code keeps being rejected
body: Symptoms: You type the six-digit code from the authenticator app at sign-in, but the page says the code is invalid or expired. Cause: The clock on your phone is out of sync with the company login system, so the codes it shows no longer match. Steps: 1. Open the authenticator app and wait for a fresh code to appear, then type it right away. 2. If it still fails, open your phone settings and turn on automatic date and time. 3. Restart the authenticator app and try a new code. 4. If the code still fails, sign out of the login page, close the browser completely, and start sign-in again. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with your name, the time you tried, and the name of the app you are using. Never share your codes with anyone, including colleagues, even if they say they are from IT.

title: Sign-in blocked after replacing your phone
body: Symptoms: You got a new phone or lost your old one, and you can no longer receive approval codes or prompts for the company login. Cause: The authenticator app was set up on the old phone, so the new phone does not have the security link for your account. Steps: 1. Do not keep guessing codes or retrying on the login page. 2. If you saved backup codes when you first set up multi-factor sign-in, use one now. 3. If you have no backup code, ask the IT help desk to reset your multi-factor setup. They will verify your identity first. 4. After the reset, install the authenticator app on your new phone and scan the new setup code shown on your computer. 5. Test sign-in on your laptop and confirm the new phone works. 6. If the lost phone was company-issued, report it to the help desk as well. Still stuck? Call the help desk from a colleague's phone or desk line, since you cannot receive codes on the lost device.

title: Approval prompt never appears on your phone
body: Symptoms: You enter your password on the sign-in page, but the approval request never shows up on your phone. Cause: Notifications are turned off for the authenticator app, the phone is in silent or focus mode, or the phone has no internet connection. Steps: 1. Check your phone has internet access by opening a web page. 2. Open phone settings, find the authenticator app, and make sure notifications are allowed. 3. Turn off focus or do not disturb mode for a moment. 4. Open the authenticator app directly, since it may show the pending request there. 5. On the sign-in page, choose the option to resend the request, then wait thirty seconds. 6. If nothing appears, choose the option to enter a code from the app instead. Still stuck? Contact the help desk and tell them whether the phone is company-issued or your own personal phone.

title: Security key not recognized by the browser
body: Symptoms: When you insert or tap your security key, the browser says no key was found, or the sign-in process stalls. Cause: The key is not fully plugged in, the browser is blocking it, or the key was never registered to your account. Steps: 1. Unplug the key and plug it into a different USB port, pushing it in firmly. 2. If your key uses wireless connection, make sure it is turned on and held close to the device. 3. Close all browser windows and open the login page again. 4. Allow the browser to use the key if it asks for permission. 5. Try a browser that the company supports, as listed on the help desk page. 6. If the key is still not found, use another sign-in method such as the authenticator app code. Still stuck? Contact the help desk so they can check whether your key is registered. Do not mail your key to anyone.

title: Text message code never arrives
body: Symptoms: You request a code by text message, but nothing arrives after several minutes. Cause: Your cell signal is weak, the phone number on file is out of date, or your mobile carrier is delaying messages. Steps: 1. Wait two minutes and check your messages, including any spam or blocked folder. 2. Restart your phone to refresh the cell signal. 3. Move to a place with better signal, or turn on Wi-Fi calling if your phone supports it. 4. On the sign-in page, request the code only once more, since repeated requests can lead to a temporary lock. 5. Check that the phone number in your profile is current, and ask the help desk to update it if it is not. 6. Switch to the authenticator app, which does not depend on cell signal. Still stuck? The help desk can arrange another verification method after confirming your identity.

title: Account locked after too many wrong codes
body: Symptoms: The sign-in page says your account is temporarily locked after several incorrect codes were entered. Cause: Too many wrong codes were entered in a short time, which triggers an automatic lock to protect your account. Steps: 1. Stop trying. Each extra attempt can extend the lock. 2. Wait fifteen minutes, then close all browser windows. 3. Make sure your phone clock is set to automatic and that you are using the correct username. 4. Open the authenticator app and wait for a new code to appear before typing it. 5. If you are still locked after the wait, contact the help desk. 6. Once you are back in, change your password if you think someone else tried to sign in. Still stuck? Give the help desk your username and the approximate time you were locked out. They can unlock your account after verifying who you are.

title: Unexpected approval requests on your phone
body: Symptoms: Your phone shows sign-in approval requests that you did not start. Cause: Someone may know your password and is trying to sign in to your account. Steps: 1. Tap deny or decline on every request you did not start. 2. Change your password right away from a computer you trust. 3. Report the event to the help desk, including the time the requests appeared. 4. Never approve a request to help someone else, even if they say it is urgent. 5. Open your account security page and remove any devices or sign-in methods you do not recognize. 6. The help desk may review recent sign-in activity with you. Still stuck? Call the help desk rather than replying by email or chat, since the message could be part of the attempt. Keep the phone and your password private.

title: Backup codes rejected at sign-in
body: Symptoms: You enter a backup code at sign-in, and the page says it is invalid. Cause: The code was already used, was typed incorrectly, or came from an older set that was replaced. Steps: 1. Check that you typed the code exactly, including any dashes, and that letters are not confused with numbers. 2. Try the next unused code on your list, since each backup code works only once. 3. Make sure you are using the most recent list you saved or printed. 4. Cross off each code as you use it so you do not try it again. 5. If none of the codes work, use the authenticator app or your security key instead. 6. After signing in, open security settings and generate a new set of backup codes, then store them somewhere safe. Still stuck? The help desk can issue a new set after verifying your identity. Never store backup codes in a shared file or sticky note on your desk.

title: New laptop setup fails during enrollment
body: Symptoms: When setting up multi-factor sign-in on a new laptop, the setup page says the device cannot be added. Cause: Setup was started in an unapproved browser, or the setup link or code expired before it was finished. Steps: 1. Sign in from your phone or an existing trusted computer first. 2. Open security settings and choose the option to add a new sign-in method. 3. Use the company-approved browser, which the help desk can confirm for you. 4. Scan the setup code with the authenticator app, then type the fresh code shown on the screen. 5. If the link has expired, request a new one and finish within ten minutes. 6. Remove old entries for laptops you no longer use so your account stays tidy. Still stuck? Contact the help desk with the name of the new laptop and the exact error message shown on the screen.

title: Authenticator app deleted or reinstalled by accident
body: Symptoms: You reinstalled or accidentally deleted the authenticator app, and your account no longer shows a code for sign-in. Cause: Deleting the app removes the stored codes unless the app was backed up before the removal. Steps: 1. Do not uninstall or reinstall the app again until you are signed in. 2. Sign in using a saved backup code or another approved method, such as a security key. 3. Once you are in, open security settings and remove the old authenticator entry. 4. Add a new entry by scanning the new setup code shown on your computer with the reinstalled app. 5. Generate and save a fresh set of backup codes in a safe place. 6. Turn on the app's cloud backup only if company policy allows it. Still stuck? The help desk can reset your authenticator setup after verifying your identity, so have your manager's name ready if asked.

title: Time on your phone is wrong and codes fail
body:
Symptoms: Your authenticator app shows a six-digit code, but the sign-in page says the code is invalid, even when you type it quickly. The codes may change faster than you can enter them, or they may never match what a colleague sees.

Cause: Authenticator codes depend on the clock in your phone being accurate. If the phone's time drifts, the codes it generates no longer match the ones the company system expects.

Steps:
1. Open the settings on your phone and find the date and time section.
2. Turn on the option that sets the time and time zone automatically.
3. Wait about thirty seconds, then open the authenticator app.
4. Look for a time correction or sync option inside the app and run it if it is there.
5. Close the app completely and open it again.
6. Try a fresh code on the sign-in page. Wait for a new code if the first one fails.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them the time shown on your phone, the name of the sign-in page, and whether a colleague's codes work for the same account.

title: Sign-in codes work on the old laptop but not the new one
body:
Symptoms: You sign in on your desk computer using the verification code from your phone without trouble. On a second device you use for work, the sign-in page never offers the option to enter a code, or it asks you to set up the app again.

Cause: Each device must be registered separately for the verification system. A second device that was never added, or was added with a different account, will not receive the setup information it needs.

Steps:
1. Sign out of the second device completely.
2. Open the sign-in page and choose the option to add a new device or set up verification.
3. Confirm your identity using your primary device if asked.
4. Scan the setup code shown on the screen with your authenticator app.
5. Enter the six-digit code from the app to finish linking the device.
6. Sign out and sign in again to confirm the new device works.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Tell them which device you are using, whether it is a work or personal machine, and the exact message shown on the sign-in page.

title: Verification prompt arrives but the Yes button does nothing
body:
Symptoms: A sign-in approval request appears on your phone, but when you tap Approve nothing happens. The request may disappear, or the spinner keeps turning and the computer never moves past the sign-in screen.

Cause: The approval request needs a working internet connection and the verification app must be up to date. A weak connection or an old app version can stop the response from reaching the system.

Steps:
1. Check that your phone has a working connection by opening a web page in your browser.
2. Switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data once to refresh the link.
3. Open the app store on your phone and install any pending update for the authenticator app.
4. Restart your phone.
5. On your computer, go back to the sign-in page and start the sign-in again from the beginning.
6. When the request arrives, open the notification and tap Approve within the time limit shown.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Mention whether the request appeared, what happened after you tapped Approve, and the type of connection your phone was using.

title: Verification app asks for a code every time you open it
body:
Symptoms: The authenticator app locks itself and asks for your phone passcode, fingerprint or face scan every time you switch to it, even within a few minutes. You may also be asked to sign in again to the app itself.

Cause: The app is set to lock aggressively, or your phone's screen lock settings have changed. This is a setting problem, not a problem with your account.

Steps:
1. Open the authenticator app and go to its settings.
2. Look for the option named app lock or security and review the timeout.
3. Set the timeout to a longer period that suits your work pattern.
4. Open your phone settings and check the screen lock timeout.
5. Make sure biometric unlock for the authenticator app is turned on, if your phone supports it.
6. Close the app and open it again to confirm the new setting is saved.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Say which phone model you use and whether the lock appears only in the authenticator app or across your whole phone.

title: Sign-in asks for a code from an app you no longer have
body:
Symptoms: The sign-in page asks for a code from an app you do not recognise, or it refers to a verification method you never set up. The list of methods shown does not include the one you use.

Cause: Your account may have been set up with more than one verification method over time. Old methods can remain on the account even after you stop using them, and the sign-in page may show the wrong one first.

Steps:
1. On the sign-in page, look for a link such as Use a different method or Choose another way.
2. Select the method you actually use, such as your authenticator app.
3. If none of the options match, select the option to get help signing in.
4. Use a backup option you have set up, such as a backup code or a message to your registered number.
5. Once signed in, open your security settings and review the list of verification methods.
6. Remove any old method you no longer use and keep your current one.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Describe the wording on the sign-in page and which method you normally use, so they can check your account.

title: Security key works on one site but not another
body:
Symptoms: Your security key lights up and asks you to touch it when you sign in to one work page, but on a different work page the key is not offered at all, or the browser says the key cannot be used.

Cause: Some sign-in pages accept only certain kinds of security keys or require the key to be registered with that specific page. The browser also may block the key if its settings are restricted.

Steps:
1. Make sure the key is firmly plugged into a working port or paired with your computer over Bluetooth.
2. Open the sign-in page that fails and look for a message about key support or an unsupported method.
3. Use a current version of the browser you normally use for work.
4. Check the browser's security or privacy settings for any rule that blocks external keys.
5. Sign in on the page that worked first to confirm the key itself is healthy.
6. Ask the IT help desk whether the failing page needs the key registered separately.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Tell them the name of the page that fails, the browser version, and whether the key is plugged in or wireless.

title: Verification request came from a stranger's sign-in attempt
body:
Symptoms: You receive an approval request on your phone for a sign-in you did not start. You may see a location, device or browser you do not recognise. You are not sure whether to tap Approve or Deny.

Cause: Someone may know your username and password and is trying to sign in as you. The request is asking for your approval so they can get past the second step.

Steps:
1. Tap Deny or Decline on the request. Do not approve it.
2. Do not reply to any message asking you to confirm or share a code.
3. Change your work password from a device you trust.
4. Open the authenticator app and check for any other pending requests, and deny them too.
5. Make a note of the time and details of the request.
6. Report the attempt to the IT help desk as soon as possible.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk right away, even if you are not certain it was an attack. Say what you saw, when it happened, and whether you already entered your password for any unknown sign-in.

title: Verification pop-up appears during a video call
body:
Symptoms: While you are on a video call or presenting your screen, your phone or computer shows a verification request that you cannot easily answer. The call freezes or you miss the prompt while sharing.

Cause: Your work account is asking for a fresh sign-in, often because the session has expired or the system needs to re-check your identity. Screen sharing can hide the prompt from you.

Steps:
1. Finish or pause the call if you can, then check your phone for the request.
2. Approve the request if you started the sign-in yourself and recognise the device.
3. If you are in a meeting, ask a colleague to take over sharing while you respond.
4. Once the call ends, sign out and sign back in to refresh your session.
5. Turn on notifications for the authenticator app so requests show on your lock screen.
6. If prompts keep interrupting you, ask the IT help desk to review your session length.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Tell them the time of the call, the app or tool you were using, and whether the prompt came to your phone or your computer.

title: Sign-in fails after your work email password changed
body:
Symptoms: You changed your work password recently and now your email app, the chat app and the company VPN app all ask you to sign in again. The verification code is accepted, but the password is refused.

Cause: Several apps store the old password. Until each one is updated, they keep trying the old password, which the system rejects before the verification step is even reached.

Steps:
1. Close all work apps completely on your phone and computer.
2. Sign out of your email app and remove the saved account from the app.
3. Add the account back using your new password.
4. Enter the verification code when asked.
5. Repeat the same process for the chat app and the company VPN app.
6. Restart your computer and check that every app signs in without errors.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. List the apps that still ask for the old password and the time you last changed your password.

title: Phone number on file no longer receives verification messages
body:
Symptoms: You are signing in and choose the option to receive a verification message on your phone number. The message never arrives, or it arrives for a number you no longer use.

Cause: The phone number stored on your account may be out of date, for example after a change of mobile provider, a new SIM card or a switch to a different number.

Steps:
1. On the sign-in page, choose the option for another way to verify, if available.
2. Use your authenticator app or a backup code to complete the sign-in.
3. Once signed in, open your security or profile settings.
4. Find the phone number field and replace the old number with your current one.
5. Confirm the new number by entering the code sent to it.
6. Remove any old numbers you no longer use from the list.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Explain that your number has changed and which verification method you can still use, so they can update your record.

title: VPN Fails After a Password Change
body: Symptoms: The company VPN app says your username or password is incorrect, even though you are sure you typed your new password correctly. Sometimes it asks for your password again and again without ever connecting. Cause: Your laptop or phone may still be saving your old password, or the VPN app has stored outdated sign-in details from before the change. Steps: 1. Close the VPN app completely, including any icon in the system tray or menu bar at the top or bottom of your screen. 2. Sign in to the staff web portal in your browser to confirm your new password works there. 3. Open the VPN app, choose Sign Out or Forget Account if you see that option, and remove any saved password. 4. Restart your laptop or phone. 5. Open the VPN app again and type your username and new password slowly, checking for caps lock and typing errors. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Tell them the time you changed your password, the exact error message you see, and whether the staff web portal works for you.

title: VPN Connects but No Websites Load
body: Symptoms: The company VPN app shows a status of Connected, but your web browser cannot open any websites, and your email app may refuse to send or receive messages. Cause: The VPN connection is up, but your laptop is still sending its internet traffic through a different network path, or an old network setting is blocking the connection. Steps: 1. Click the VPN app and select Disconnect, then wait about thirty seconds. 2. Turn your Wi-Fi off and back on, or unplug and reconnect your network cable. 3. Open your web browser and try to load any public website while disconnected, to confirm your basic internet works. 4. Connect to the VPN again and wait until it shows Connected for at least one full minute. 5. Try the internal staff site first, then a public website. 6. If nothing loads, restart your laptop with the VPN app still disconnected, then reconnect. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and mention which Wi-Fi network you are using and whether the problem happens at home, at the office, or both.

title: Authenticator Code Rejected at VPN Sign-In
body: Symptoms: When you sign in to the VPN, the sign-in screen asks for a six-digit code from the authenticator app, but it keeps saying the code is invalid or expired. Cause: The clock on your phone or the clock on your laptop may be out of sync, or you may be typing a code that has already expired. Codes change about every thirty seconds. Steps: 1. Wait until the authenticator app shows a fresh code with plenty of time left, ideally more than ten seconds. 2. Type the code carefully, without spaces, and submit it right away. 3. If it still fails, open the settings in the authenticator app and check that automatic time or network time is turned on. 4. Restart your phone so it updates its clock. 5. Make sure you are using the account entry for the company VPN, not a personal account with a similar name. 6. Try signing in again with a new code. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Do not share your codes with anyone. Staff will check whether your authenticator needs to be set up again.

title: VPN Keeps Dropping Every Few Minutes
body: Symptoms: The company VPN app connects normally, but after a few minutes it disconnects by itself. You may need to sign in again several times during a single work session, and open files may stop saving. Cause: Weak or unstable Wi-Fi, a sleeping laptop, or a power-saving setting on your network adapter can interrupt the VPN connection without warning. Steps: 1. Move closer to your Wi-Fi router or switch to a wired network cable if one is available. 2. Close large downloads, video calls, and streaming programs while you work remotely. 3. Open your laptop power settings and set it so the computer does not sleep while plugged in during your working hours. 4. Restart your laptop and connect to the VPN before opening other work programs. 5. Keep the VPN app updated by accepting updates when the app prompts you. 6. Save your work often while you test the connection. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Mention how often the drops happen, what you were doing at the time, and whether the problem happens on other Wi-Fi networks too.

title: Remote Desktop to Office Computer Refuses to Connect
body: Symptoms: You are connected to the company VPN app, but when you try to open your office computer using the remote desktop app, you see messages such as Connection failed or The remote computer could not be reached. Cause: Your office computer may be turned off, asleep, or locked into a state that does not accept remote connections. The computer name you typed may also be wrong. Steps: 1. Check with a colleague in the office, or ask someone to confirm your office computer is turned on and not in sleep mode. 2. Confirm you are still connected to the VPN, since remote desktop needs the VPN to reach office machines. 3. Type the computer name exactly as written on your remote access instructions, with no extra spaces. 4. Close the remote desktop app and open it again. 5. Try connecting again and enter your work username and password when asked. 6. If you see a certificate warning, do not accept it unless the help desk has told you it is expected. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Include the exact message you see and the name of the computer you are trying to reach.

title: VPN Is Very Slow Compared to Normal
body: Symptoms: Web pages, email, and shared files take a long time to load while you are connected to the company VPN app. Video calls may freeze or sound robotic, even though your home internet seems fine for other devices. Cause: VPN traffic travels through the company network, so slow speeds can come from your home connection, a busy Wi-Fi channel, or many devices sharing the same internet line at once. Steps: 1. Run a quick speed check in your web browser with no VPN connected to see your normal home internet speed. 2. Pause downloads, cloud backups, and streaming on other devices in your home. 3. Move closer to your Wi-Fi router, or connect your laptop with a network cable. 4. Restart your home router by unplugging it for thirty seconds, then plugging it back in. 5. Close extra browser tabs and programs that use the internet, such as music or photo sync tools. 6. Reconnect to the VPN and test a small webpage before opening large files. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Share your speed check results and what time of day the slowness happens, so the team can look for network problems.

title: VPN Shows a Certificate Expired Error
body: Symptoms: When you open the company VPN app, you see a warning that a security certificate has expired or is not trusted, and the app will not connect until you deal with the warning. Cause: The VPN app uses a digital security file, called a certificate, to prove it is talking to the real company network. These files expire on a set date, and an out-of-date laptop clock can also make a valid certificate look expired. Steps: 1. Check the date and time on your laptop or phone and turn on automatic date and time. 2. Restart the computer so the correct date is applied. 3. Open the VPN app and check for an update, then install it if one is available. 4. If the warning still appears, do not click through it on your own. Take a screenshot of the message showing the expiry date. 5. Try the company staff web portal in your browser to see whether it shows a similar warning. 6. Wait for guidance from IT before trying any other fix. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and send the screenshot, along with the date and time shown on your laptop.

title: Account Locked After Several Failed VPN Attempts
body: Symptoms: The company VPN app says your account is locked or temporarily disabled after you tried to sign in several times. Even the correct password does not work, and you may also be unable to sign in to your email app. Cause: For security, the company locks accounts after a set number of failed sign-in attempts. Attempts can fail because of an old saved password on another device, such as a phone email app or a tablet, which keeps trying in the background. Steps: 1. Stop trying to sign in, because each attempt may extend the lock period. 2. Check your phone, tablet, and any other laptop for email or VPN apps that might still have an old password saved. 3. Update or sign out of those apps so they stop sending the old password. 4. Wait the time shown in the error message, which is often fifteen to thirty minutes. 5. After the wait, sign in once on the staff web portal with your current password. 6. If the lock remains, do not keep trying. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Staff can confirm your account status and unlock it safely after checking for suspicious activity.

title: VPN Works at Home but Not on Public Wi-Fi
body: Symptoms: The company VPN app connects smoothly at home, but when you travel or work from a hotel, cafe, airport, or conference center, it fails to connect or shows a timeout message. Cause: Public Wi-Fi networks often have sign-in pages that must be completed before the internet works, and some block the special traffic that VPN apps use. Steps: 1. Connect to the public Wi-Fi network and open your web browser. 2. If a sign-in or terms page appears, accept the terms or enter the code provided by the venue. 3. Load any public website to confirm the network is fully open. 4. Open the VPN app and connect once the basic website loads. 5. If the VPN still fails, switch to your phone as a personal hotspot and connect the laptop to that instead. 6. Avoid public networks that show no password and no sign-in page, since they may be unsafe. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Tell them the name of the venue, the network you used, and the exact message the VPN app displayed.

title: VPN App Will Not Open at All
body: Symptoms: When you click the company VPN app, nothing happens. The window may flash and close, or it stays on the loading screen with no sign-in box. You may not see any error message at all. Cause: The VPN app is stuck in a background process from an earlier session, or a recent update did not finish installing. Your laptop may also be waiting for a restart after updates. Steps: 1. Right-click the VPN app icon in the taskbar or menu bar and choose Quit, then open it again. 2. If it still does not open, restart your laptop and try once more. 3. Check for updates in the company software center and install any pending VPN app update. 4. Once the update finishes, restart the laptop again. 5. If the app still does not open, uninstall it from Settings or Control Panel, then reinstall it from the company software center. 6. Sign in with your usual work account and approve the sign-in on your authenticator app. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and include the version number shown under the VPN app's Help menu, plus whether the app shows any message before it closes.

title: Shared Drive Will Not Open While on VPN
body:
Symptoms: You are connected to the company VPN app and it shows connected. Your shared drive folders show an error saying the path is not available, or they stay blank. Email and internal web pages may still work.

Cause: The shared drive is reached by a network name that your laptop cannot resolve while connected through the VPN. This often happens when your laptop still uses an old saved drive mapping, or the VPN app is set to send only some traffic through the tunnel.

Steps:
1. Disconnect from the VPN app, then reconnect and wait for the connected message.
2. Open File Explorer or Finder and remove any old mapped drive that shows a red X.
3. Add the drive again using the path given in the shared drive guide on the intranet.
4. If it still fails, restart your laptop while connected to the VPN.
5. Note the exact error text and the time it happened.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk through the chat app or call the service desk line. Include the folder path you tried, your laptop model, and the error text. Never share your password in messages.

title: VPN Sign-In Page Shows a Blank White Screen
body:
Symptoms: When you open the VPN app and choose sign-in, a white or empty window appears. No sign-in boxes show up. A spinning circle may keep turning and never finish.

Cause: The sign-in page is shown inside a small built-in browser window. Outdated browser components, a blocked security add-on, or a stuck background process can stop the page from drawing.

Steps:
1. Close the VPN app completely, including its icon in the system tray or menu bar.
2. Wait thirty seconds, then open the VPN app again.
3. Try the sign-in page once more and wait up to two minutes.
4. Restart your laptop, then try again.
5. If a pop-up blocker or security add-on appears, allow the VPN sign-in page.
6. Check that the VPN app is up to date from the software center.

Still stuck? Try signing in from another browser using the self-service portal link on the intranet. If that works, report the problem so IT can update the VPN app. Share the app version number shown under Help or About.

title: VPN App Says Update Required Before Connecting
body:
Symptoms: A message says your VPN app is out of date and must be updated before you can connect. The connect button is grey or does nothing. Colleagues with the same laptop model may see the same message.

Cause: IT sets a minimum version for the VPN app for security reasons. Older versions are blocked from connecting until they are updated.

Steps:
1. Read the message and note the required version number.
2. Open the software center or company app store on your laptop.
3. Search for the VPN app and select Update.
4. If no update is listed, choose Check for updates from the VPN app menu.
5. Restart the laptop after the update finishes.
6. Open the VPN app and sign in as normal.

Still stuck? If the update button is missing or the install fails, contact the IT help desk and tell them which version you have. Only use the company software center to install the app. Do not download it from a website you found by search.

title: Remote Desktop Connects but Screen Stays Black
body:
Symptoms: The remote desktop app connects to your office computer and a window opens, but the screen is black or shows only the wallpaper with no icons. The mouse may move, but nothing responds. Sometimes a message says the session is still starting.

Cause: The office computer may be locked, asleep, or stuck in a session that did not finish starting. Someone else may still be signed in there, or the display size does not match your window.

Steps:
1. Wait two minutes, then press any key or move the mouse.
2. Close the remote session window and open it again from the remote desktop app.
3. If you see a sign-in prompt, enter your normal password and approve any authenticator prompt.
4. Press Ctrl+Alt+Del in the window, choose Task Manager, and check that it responds.
5. If the screen is still black, change the display size to a smaller setting in the remote desktop app menu.
6. Ask a colleague in the office to check that the computer is awake and not locked by someone else.

Still stuck? Call the IT help desk and give them the office computer name, the time you tried, and whether anyone else was signed in. Always lock the office computer when you finish working on it.

title: Authenticator Codes Rejected Because Phone Clock Is Off
body:
Symptoms: The authenticator app shows six-digit codes, but they are rejected at sign-in even when typed quickly. Codes may work on another phone or on another day. Your phone may have been restarted or moved to a new time zone recently.

Cause: Authenticator codes change every thirty seconds and depend on the phone clock being correct. If the phone clock drifts by more than a minute, the code no longer matches the one the company expects.

Steps:
1. On your phone, open the date and time settings.
2. Turn on automatic date and time, and automatic time zone.
3. Close the authenticator app fully and reopen it.
4. Wait for a fresh code to appear, then type it straight away.
5. Try the VPN sign-in again with the new code.
6. If the problem continues, restart the phone.

Still stuck? Stop trying codes, because too many failed attempts can lock your account. Contact the IT help desk and mention that your phone clock was recently changed. Never share your authenticator codes with anyone, including IT staff.

title: VPN Says Device Is Not Approved for Remote Access
body:
Symptoms: After entering your password and code, the VPN app says this device is not approved for remote access. Your personal computer may work fine on other sites. The message often appears on a new or rebuilt laptop.

Cause: The company only allows remote access from devices that IT has registered and checked for security. A new, rebuilt, or personal device will not be on the approved list yet.

Steps:
1. Check that you are using your company laptop, not a personal device.
2. Note the device name shown in the VPN app error details.
3. Connect the laptop to the normal office or home network and keep it online.
4. Submit a device registration request through the IT service portal.
5. Include the device name, and your manager's approval if the form asks for it.
6. Wait for the confirmation email before trying the VPN again.

Still stuck? Call the IT help desk if approval has been pending more than one working day. Give them the device name and request number. Do not use a personal device to get around the block, because this breaks company security rules.

title: Printer Not Found While Connected to VPN
body:
Symptoms: While connected to the VPN, your computer cannot find the office printer. The print queue shows an error, or the printer is missing from the list. Printing works fine when you are in the office.

Cause: Office printers sit on the internal office network. Some VPN setups only carry work web and file traffic, so local printers cannot be reached from outside the office.

Steps:
1. Check that the VPN app shows connected.
2. Use the secure print or print-to-email option in the company print portal if one is offered.
3. Save the document as a PDF and send it to yourself by email.
4. Print the file from the office the next time you are in.
5. Ask IT whether a remote print queue can be added for your team.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk through the chat app. Give them the printer name, your building, and the type of document you need to print. Do not install printer drivers from unknown websites.

title: VPN Drops Only After Laptop Wakes From Sleep
body:
Symptoms: The VPN connects normally in the morning, but after you close the lid and reopen it, the VPN shows disconnected and websites or drives stop working. Reconnecting may take a minute. The problem happens after sleep, not during active use.

Cause: When a laptop sleeps, its network connection pauses. On waking, the VPN app may not restore the tunnel automatically, especially if the Wi-Fi reconnects slowly or the VPN app is set to end after idle time.

Steps:
1. After opening the lid, wait thirty seconds for the Wi-Fi icon to show connected.
2. Open the VPN app and click Connect if it shows disconnected.
3. Check the VPN app settings and turn off any option that disconnects on sleep.
4. Restart the laptop at least once a day, especially after updates.
5. Keep the VPN app open in the background rather than quitting it.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk if the VPN drops several times a day after sleep. Mention your laptop model and whether you use office Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot. Do not leave the VPN switched off to avoid the problem.

title: Internal Tools Ask You to Log In Again While on VPN
body:
Symptoms: The VPN shows connected and you can open email, but internal tools such as the timesheet or leave system keep asking you to sign in again. The login box may appear again after a few clicks, even though you just entered your details.

Cause: Internal tools use their own session cookies. If your browser has blocked cookies, is using an old saved login, or has a stale session from before a password change, the tool will keep asking for sign-in.

Steps:
1. Open the internal tool in a private or incognito browser window.
2. Sign in once, and approve any authenticator prompt.
3. If it works in a private window, clear saved cookies for the internal site in your browser settings.
4. Close all browser windows and open the tool again.
5. Make sure your browser allows cookies from the company intranet.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and name the tool that keeps asking for sign-in. Say whether it works in a private window. Do not save your password in the browser on shared computers.

title: Connection Times Out When Using a Phone Hotspot
body:
Symptoms: When you connect your laptop to the internet through your phone's hotspot and then start the VPN, the connection stays on connecting for a long time and then fails with a timeout message. The same VPN works on office or home Wi-Fi.

Cause: Phone hotspots can be slow or limited, and some mobile networks block or limit the traffic that VPN apps use. The signal strength or data limit on your phone can also cause a timeout.

Steps:
1. Check that your phone has a strong mobile signal and data left on the plan.
2. Move closer to a window or step outside if the signal is weak.
3. Turn the hotspot off and on again, then reconnect the laptop.
4. Start the VPN app and wait up to two minutes before trying again.
5. If it still fails, switch to a different Wi-Fi network if one is available.

Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and say which mobile network you use and what time it failed. Do not rely on a hotspot for long work sessions, as a stable connection is needed for remote access.

title: Email not syncing on your phone
body:
Symptoms:
New messages show up on your laptop but not on your phone. Sent messages may not appear in the Sent folder, and the inbox may be days behind.

Cause:
The phone's mail app has lost its connection to the company mail server, often after a password change, a long period offline, or a software update.

Steps:
1. Make sure your phone has a working Wi-Fi or mobile data connection.
2. Open your email app and pull down on the inbox to refresh it.
3. Go to the account settings and check that the email address and password are correct.
4. If you changed your password recently, remove the account from the phone and add it again using the new password.
5. Restart the phone and check the inbox again.
6. Confirm that the phone date and time are set to automatic.

Still stuck?
Contact the IT help desk and tell them your phone model, the email app name, and whether the problem started after a password change.

title: Cannot send email with attachment
body:
Symptoms:
You write an email, add a file, and press send. The message stays in the Outbox or returns with an error saying the message is too large.

Cause:
Most company email accounts limit the total size of a message, including all attachments, to a fixed amount. Large videos, scanned folders, or many photos can go over that limit.

Steps:
1. Check the size of each file. Right-click it on your laptop and look at the size in its properties.
2. Remove the largest attachments from the message.
3. Compress the files into a single zip folder if they are documents or photos.
4. For files larger than the limit, upload them to the company file share and send a link instead.
5. Make sure you are connected to the internet, then try sending again.
6. Check the Outbox and delete any stuck copies before resending.

Still stuck?
If the attachment is essential and you cannot share it through the file share, contact the IT help desk for help sending it securely.

title: Missing emails in your inbox
body:
Symptoms:
You expect an email from a colleague or customer, but it does not appear in your inbox. You may find it hours or days later in another folder, or not at all.

Cause:
The message may have been moved by a rule, filtered into the junk folder, or archived automatically. Sometimes a rule was created by accident or a mailbox setting changed.

Steps:
1. Use the search box at the top of your email app and type the sender's name or part of the subject line.
2. Check the Junk or Spam folder and the Deleted Items folder.
3. If you find the message, drag it back to the inbox and mark it as safe.
4. Open the settings and review your inbox rules to see if any rule moves messages automatically.
5. Ask the sender to resend the message and confirm they used the correct address.
6. Check the Archive folder if your app has one.

Still stuck?
Contact the IT help desk with the sender's address, the approximate date sent, and the subject line so they can trace the message.

title: Calendar invitations not showing up
body:
Symptoms:
Colleagues tell you they sent you a meeting invitation, but it does not appear in your calendar. You may also miss updates to meetings you already accepted.

Cause:
Invitations often arrive in your inbox first and must be accepted before they are added to your calendar. Some invitations are also blocked or filtered when the sender uses an outside calendar service.

Steps:
1. Search your inbox for the meeting title or the word invitation.
2. Open the invitation email and check whether it asks you to accept, tentatively accept, or decline.
3. Select Accept so the meeting is added to your calendar.
4. Open your calendar app and check that the correct calendar is ticked in the list on the side.
5. If the meeting is still missing, ask the organizer to send the invitation again.
6. Refresh the calendar app by closing it and opening it again.

Still stuck?
Contact the IT help desk with the meeting title, the organizer's name, and the date and time of the meeting.

title: Out-of-office reply not working
body:
Symptoms:
You are on leave, but people who email you do not receive an automatic reply. Or the reply is sent to people outside the company when you only wanted it to go to colleagues.

Cause:
The out-of-office setting is turned off, has an end date that has already passed, or is set to reply only to contacts inside the company.

Steps:
1. Open your email app and go to the settings menu.
2. Find the automatic replies or out-of-office option.
3. Turn on the setting and type your message.
4. Check the start and end dates and correct them if needed.
5. Choose whether replies go to everyone or only to people inside the company.
6. Select Save and send a test email from another account to confirm it works.

Still stuck?
If the option is missing or greyed out, contact the IT help desk and tell them your email app version and the device you are using.

title: Cannot log in to your email account
body:
Symptoms:
The email app keeps asking for your password, shows an error that the password is wrong, or says the account is locked. You may be unable to open your email on any device.

Cause:
Your password may have expired, been mistyped, or been changed on another device. After several failed attempts, the account can be locked for security reasons.

Steps:
1. Check that Caps Lock is off and type your password slowly.
2. Try logging in to the company web portal in a browser to confirm your password works.
3. If the portal says your password has expired, follow the prompts to set a new one.
4. Wait fifteen minutes before trying again if you see a message about too many attempts.
5. Update the saved password on your phone and laptop after you change it.
6. Restart the device and try the email app again.

Still stuck?
Contact the IT help desk. Do not keep trying passwords, as this can extend the lock. Staff may need to verify your identity before unlocking the account.

title: Shared mailbox not appearing
body:
Symptoms:
You were told you have access to a team mailbox, such as a general support address, but it does not show in your email app. You may see the messages only in a web browser.

Cause:
Access was granted but the account has not been added to your email app, or the app needs a restart to show new access.

Steps:
1. Open your email app and check the list of folders or accounts on the side.
2. Look for an option to add a shared or additional mailbox.
3. Type the full address of the shared mailbox and select Add.
4. Close and reopen the email app.
5. Log in to the web portal in a browser and check whether the shared mailbox appears there.
6. If it appears in the browser but not the app, remove and re-add it in the app settings.

Still stuck?
Contact the IT help desk and give them the exact name of the shared mailbox and your own work email address so they can confirm your access.

title: Emails sent to wrong person
body:
Symptoms:
You sent an email to the wrong recipient, or you added a person to the copy line by mistake. You want to stop the message from reaching them or limit the damage.

Cause:
Email is delivered quickly once sent, and most email apps cannot reliably recall a message after it has been delivered to another person's inbox.

Steps:
1. Act quickly and check whether your app shows an Undo Send option at the bottom of the screen.
2. If the message is still in your Outbox, open it and delete it.
3. If the message was delivered, do not send more emails about it until you have a plan.
4. Contact the wrong recipient politely and ask them to delete the message without reading further.
5. Check the message for personal or confidential information and note what was shared.
6. Write down the date, time, and recipient address for your records.

Still stuck?
Report the mistake to the IT help desk right away, especially if the email contained personal or customer information. Quick reporting helps the company meet its data protection duties.

title: Cannot open meeting link in calendar
body:
Symptoms:
A meeting entry in your calendar has a video link, but clicking it does nothing, shows an error, or opens a page saying the meeting cannot be found.

Cause:
The link may be out of date because the meeting was moved or cancelled, the link was copied incorrectly, or the video app is not installed or is blocked on your laptop.

Steps:
1. Open the calendar entry and read the meeting time to confirm it is still scheduled.
2. Copy the link and paste it into a web browser instead of clicking it.
3. Check that the video app is installed and up to date on your laptop.
4. Restart your browser and try the link again.
5. Ask the organizer to send the latest link by email.
6. If you are using a phone, try joining from the video app itself.

Still stuck?
Contact the IT help desk before the meeting starts. Give them the meeting title, the time, and any error message you see, so they can check the link.

title: Calendar showing wrong time zone
body:
Symptoms:
Meetings appear one or more hours earlier or later than expected. Colleagues in other offices say the times do not match what you agreed.

Cause:
The calendar or your computer is set to the wrong time zone, or the calendar has a separate time zone setting that does not match your location.

Steps:
1. Open your calendar app and go to the settings menu.
2. Find the time zone section and check that it shows your current location.
3. Change the time zone to the correct one if it is wrong.
4. Check your laptop's date and time settings and turn on automatic time zone if available.
5. Restart the calendar app and look at a meeting you know well to confirm the time is correct.
6. Tell any colleagues who sent invitations with the wrong time to confirm the meeting again.

Still stuck?
Contact the IT help desk if the time zone setting is locked or if meetings still show the wrong time after the change.

title: Email keeps disconnecting on your laptop
body: Symptoms: Your email app on your laptop shows a disconnected message every few minutes. New messages arrive only after you restart the app, and the sync icon keeps spinning. Cause: The laptop may be switching between Wi-Fi networks, or the company VPN app may be dropping the connection in the background. Steps: 1. Check that your laptop is connected to a stable Wi-Fi network and that no large download is using all the bandwidth. 2. Turn off Wi-Fi, wait ten seconds, then turn it back on. 3. Close the company VPN app completely, reopen it and sign in again. 4. Open your email app, go to Account settings and confirm the server address is unchanged. 5. Turn off any battery saver mode, which can pause background connections. 6. Restart your laptop and watch for the disconnect message over the next half hour. Still stuck? Take a screenshot of the error and note the time it appeared, then log a ticket with the IT help desk and mention whether you use a cabled or wireless connection.

title: Attachment rejected as too large
body: Symptoms: When you try to send a file, your email app shows a message saying the attachment exceeds the size limit, or the email stays in the outbox. Cause: The company mail system limits the total size of each message, usually around 20 megabytes, and files can grow once they are attached. Steps: 1. Right-click the file and check its size in its properties. 2. Compress the files into a single zip folder, which often makes them smaller. 3. For large videos or images, reduce their resolution before attaching. 4. Upload the file to the company file sharing area instead, then paste the link into your email. 5. Send the link to the recipient and ask them to confirm they can open it. 6. Delete the failed draft from the outbox so it does not retry. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them the file type, approximate size and recipient, so they can suggest a safe transfer method.

title: Calendar invitations showing twice
body: Symptoms: The same meeting appears two or three times on your calendar, sometimes with different times or titles. Cause: The invitation was accepted from both a phone and a laptop, or the meeting was sent to a shared team calendar and to you directly, so both copies sync. Steps: 1. Open one of the duplicate meetings and check the organiser name. 2. If the same organiser appears on each copy, open the invite and choose Delete from calendar, not Decline. 3. Keep the copy with the correct time and location. 4. Check your phone calendar app and remove any duplicates there too, as they may sync back. 5. Ask the organiser to resend the invite if the correct one has disappeared. 6. Confirm the meeting now appears only once. Still stuck? Send the help desk the meeting title and date, plus the names of the devices where you see the duplicates.

title: Emails landing in the junk folder
body: Symptoms: Messages from colleagues or known customers go straight to the junk folder, and you only find them when you search. Cause: The mail filter has marked the sender as suspicious, often because the message contained many links or images or came from a new address. Steps: 1. Open the junk folder and find the message. 2. Select it and choose Not junk or Move to inbox. 3. Right-click the sender name and add them to your safe senders list. 4. Check your filter rules in settings and remove any rule that moves messages from that sender. 5. Ask the sender to check that their signature and sending address look normal. 6. Wait a few hours and confirm new messages arrive in the inbox. Still stuck? Forward an example message to the help desk with the sender address and time sent, so they can check the mail system records.

title: Mailbox full warning
body: Symptoms: You see a warning that your mailbox is nearly full, and new emails may bounce back to senders. Cause: Old messages, large attachments and items in the deleted folder add up until they reach the storage limit. Steps: 1. Open your email app and sort messages by size. 2. Delete large attachments you no longer need. 3. Empty the deleted items folder. 4. Check the sent items folder for old large messages and remove them. 5. Move important older emails to an archive folder on your laptop. 6. Check the storage bar in settings and confirm it has dropped. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk before deleting anything you are unsure about, as they can check whether items must be kept for records.

title: Email signature missing on replies
body: Symptoms: Your name and job title do not appear at the bottom of emails you send from your phone or laptop, or they appear on new messages but not on replies. Cause: Signatures are set separately for each device and can be set differently for new messages and for replies and forwards. Steps: 1. Open your email app settings. 2. Find the signature section. 3. Paste your signature text into the box for new messages. 4. Tick the option to use the same signature for replies and forwards. 5. Repeat the same steps in your phone email app. 6. Send a test message to yourself and check the bottom of the message on both replies and new emails. Still stuck? Contact the help desk and tell them which devices are missing the signature.

title: Recurring meeting shows wrong dates
body: Symptoms: A weekly meeting appears on the wrong day after a certain date, or some of its later occurrences are missing from your calendar. Cause: The organiser edited only one occurrence, or changed the time zone of the series, which splits the recurring pattern. Steps: 1. Open the meeting and check the day and time of the next occurrence. 2. Ask the organiser whether they changed just one instance. 3. If you are the organiser, open the series rather than a single meeting and choose Edit series. 4. Set the correct day, time and time zone. 5. Save and choose to update all occurrences. 6. Check the next three dates to confirm they are correct. Still stuck? Send the help desk the meeting title and the dates that look wrong, and they will check the series settings for you.

title: Room booking not confirmed
body: Symptoms: You book a meeting room in your calendar, but the booking shows as pending or the room never appears in the invitation. Cause: The room is set to require approval, or the room is already booked for that time slot. Steps: 1. Open the calendar and check the room availability for your chosen time. 2. Choose a different slot or a different room if it is already taken. 3. Add the room again using the room field in the invite. 4. Check whether the room needs approval and, if so, wait for the approver to respond. 5. Send the invite again once the room shows as available. 6. Confirm the room shows as accepted in the meeting details. Still stuck? Contact the help desk with the room name, date and time, and they will check the booking system for you.

title: Email search returns no results
body: Symptoms: You type a name or subject into the search box and get no results, even though you know the email exists. Cause: The search index is still updating, or the search is limited to the current folder or to the wrong date range. Steps: 1. Clear the search box and retype the keyword. 2. Change the search scope to All mail or All folders. 3. Check the date filter and remove it. 4. Try a shorter keyword, such as only the surname of the sender. 5. Restart your email app to refresh the search index. 6. If you only recently set up the app, wait fifteen minutes and try again. Still stuck? Tell the help desk the sender, approximate date and subject so they can check the search index for your account.

title: Email stuck in the outbox
body: Symptoms: Messages you send stay in the outbox with a clock icon and never reach the recipients. Cause: Your laptop or phone is offline, your password has recently changed, or the message is too large to send. Steps: 1. Check that your device has a working internet connection. 2. Open the outbox and select the stuck message. 3. Choose Send or Retry. 4. If it fails again, sign out of the email app and sign back in. 5. Check whether you changed your password recently and, if so, enter the new one. 6. Remove any large attachment and send the message again. Still stuck? Contact the help desk with the time you sent the message and any error text shown on screen.

title: Printer shows as offline
body: Symptoms: When you send a document to print, your laptop says the printer is offline, or the print job never starts. The printer's screen may look normal but nothing comes out. Cause: The printer has lost its connection to the office network, often after a restart, a Wi-Fi drop, or a cable being bumped. Your laptop then treats it as unavailable. Steps: 1. Check that the printer is switched on and its display shows no error. 2. Confirm the network cable is firmly plugged in, or that the printer's Wi-Fi light is on. 3. Restart the printer and wait two full minutes for it to reconnect. 4. On your laptop, open the printer list in settings, select the printer, and choose the option to set it online. 5. Send a short test page to confirm. Still stuck? Restart your laptop, then contact the IT help desk with the printer name and the room number where it sits.

title: Print job stuck in the queue
body: Symptoms: Your document appears in the print list but never comes out. Other people's jobs may also be waiting behind yours, and the printer's screen may show nothing unusual. Cause: A damaged or half-sent job is blocking the line. Jobs print in order, so one stuck item holds up everything after it. Steps: 1. Open the print queue from the printer icon in the taskbar or from the printer list in settings. 2. Look for jobs that show an error or have not moved for several minutes. 3.
