Select the stuck job and choose cancel or delete. 4. If the list will not clear, choose the option to cancel all documents, then confirm. 5. Send your document again once the queue is empty. Do not resend the same file many times, because each copy adds to the jam. Still stuck? Restart the printer to clear its memory, and if the queue keeps filling up, tell the IT help desk so they can clear the print server.

title: Paper jam message will not go away
body: Symptoms: The printer shows a paper jam warning even though you cannot see any paper, or it keeps showing the message after you remove a sheet. Printing stops completely until the warning clears. Cause: A small torn piece of paper is still caught somewhere inside, often near the rollers or the back cover, and the sensor still detects it. Steps: 1. Switch the printer off and wait thirty seconds. 2. Open every access door, including the front, back, and any tray. 3. Gently pull any paper in the direction it normally travels, never against it, and slowly so it does not tear. 4. Check under the toner or ink cartridge area for scraps. 5. Close all doors firmly, switch the printer on, and print one test page. Do not use sharp tools inside the printer. Still stuck? Take a photo of the open printer and send it to the IT help desk, along with the error code shown on the screen.

title: Pages come out blank
body: Symptoms: The printer runs normally and seems to accept your job, but the pages that come out are completely white. Sometimes only the first page is blank, or the text is so faint it cannot be read. Cause: The most common reason is an empty or nearly empty ink or toner cartridge. Another cause is a print setting that tells the printer to skip the content, or a document that is set to a hidden or white layer. Steps: 1. Look at the printer's screen or the supplies panel for a low or empty cartridge warning. 2. Remove the cartridge and check it, then reseat it firmly. 3. Print a test page from the printer's own menu, not from your laptop. 4. If the test page is blank, replace the cartridge with one from the supply cupboard. 5. If the test page is fine, open your document and check it prints in the preview. Still stuck? Tell the IT help desk the printer name and which cartridge colour is affected so a replacement can be ordered.

title: Printout is cut off at the edges
body: Symptoms: Text or images run off the edge of the page, or a border is missing on one side. The printout looks fine on your screen but not on paper. Cause: The paper size in the printer does not match the size set in your document, such as letter in one and A4 in the other. A scaling setting can also shrink or enlarge the page. Steps: 1. Open the document and check the page size under the layout or page setup menu. 2. Open the print dialog and look for the paper size option. Set it to match the paper loaded in the tray. 3. Set scaling to actual size or fit to page, not custom. 4. Check that the correct paper tray is selected. 5. Print one page first to confirm the layout is right before printing the full job. Still stuck? Let the IT help desk know the document name and the paper size in the tray so they can check the printer's default settings.

title: Scans do not arrive by email
body: Symptoms: You place a document on the scanner, choose send to email, and the printer screen says the scan was sent. The email never shows up in your inbox, or it arrives hours later. Cause: The scanner may be using an outdated email account setting, or the scan may be going to a shared mailbox you do not check. Spam filters can also hold scans that contain large attachments. Steps: 1. Check your junk or spam folder for a message from the scanner name. 2. Confirm the email address on the scanner screen matches your work address exactly. 3. Scan a single page and send it again, since very large files often fail. 4. Ask a colleague to check whether a scan sent to them has arrived. 5. If nothing arrives, try scanning to a folder instead, which is covered in the next article. Still stuck? Send the IT help desk the time you scanned and the scanner name so they can check the mail server logs.

title: Scanned files go to the wrong folder
body: Symptoms: You scan a document to a network folder, but you cannot find it where you expected. The scanner says the scan succeeded. You may find it in a folder belonging to someone else, or in a folder with an unfamiliar name. Cause: Each scanner is set up with a default destination. If the scanner was set up for a different team, or the destination was changed, new scans will go there. Steps: 1. Look at the destination name shown on the scanner screen before you press start. 2. Use the scanner menu to pick your own folder from the saved list. 3. If your folder is not listed, ask the IT help desk to add it to the scanner for you. 4. Search your laptop or network drive for the file name, which often includes the date and time. 5. Move the file to the correct folder once you find it. Do not save scans to your desktop, since they can be lost when the laptop is replaced. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the scanner name and the folder you expected, so the default can be corrected.

title: Printer not found on the Wi-Fi network
body: Symptoms: When you try to add a wireless printer on your laptop, the printer does not appear in the list. Printers that worked yesterday may have disappeared, or they show up for some colleagues but not for you. Cause: Your laptop may be connected to a guest network, which is separate from the office network. Some printers also only appear when the printer and laptop are on the same network segment. Steps: 1. Check the Wi-Fi name in the corner of your laptop and make sure it says the office network, not guest. 2. Print a configuration page from the printer's menu to find its network address. 3. In your laptop's printer settings, choose to add a printer by address and enter the address from the page. 4. If the address does not work, turn Wi-Fi off and on again on your laptop. 5. Restart the printer if it has been running for weeks. Still stuck? Send the IT help desk the printer name, the address from the configuration page, and the name of the Wi-Fi network you are using.

title: Printing on the wrong paper tray
body: Symptoms: Your document prints on plain paper when you wanted letterhead, or it comes out of the large tray when you expected the small one. Sometimes the printer stops and asks you to load paper that is already loaded. Cause: The paper source in your print settings does not match what is loaded in the printer. Some printers also default to the first tray regardless of what you choose. Steps: 1. Open the print dialog and find the paper source or tray option before you press print. 2. Choose the tray that holds the paper you need, and check that the paper type matches. 3. Look at the printer screen to confirm which trays are loaded and with which paper. 4. If the printer keeps asking for paper, press the button to use the loaded tray or cancel and reprint. 5. Ask whoever refilled the paper to label the tray with its paper type. Still stuck? Tell the IT help desk which tray you need and what paper is in it so the printer defaults can be changed.

title: Double-sided printing does not work
body: Symptoms: You choose two-sided printing, but the printer only prints on one side of each page. Or the second side is printed upside down, or the pages come out with text on the wrong side. Cause: Either the printer does not have an automatic duplex unit, or the print settings are set to one side by default. Some printers also need the paper placed in a specific orientation for the second side to line up. Steps: 1. Open the print dialog and look for a two-sided or duplex option. Make sure it is turned on. 2. Choose the binding style, such as flip on long edge for normal documents. 3. Check the printer's back cover or label for a duplex symbol to confirm it supports two-sided printing. 4. If the second side is upside down, change the binding from long edge to short edge and print again. 5. If the printer has no duplex unit, print odd pages first, flip the stack, and print even pages. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and say whether the printer has a two-sided symbol, so they can check its settings.

title: Printer shows offline on only one laptop
body: Symptoms: The printer works fine from most computers, but one laptop shows it as offline and print jobs wait without printing. Cause: That laptop still has an old network address saved for the printer, often from before the printer was moved or restarted. Steps: 1. Open the printer list on your laptop and find the office printer. 2. Right-click it and choose Remove, then close the window. 3. Open the printer's network page from the printer control panel and write down its current address. 4. Add the printer again on your laptop using the printer name from the office list, not an old address. 5. Print a single test page to confirm it works. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the printer name, the laptop model, and whether other laptops print normally.

title: Printer keeps disconnecting from Wi-Fi
body: Symptoms: The printer connects to the office Wi-Fi, but after some time it disappears from your laptop and print jobs fail until it is restarted. Cause: The printer may be too far from the Wi-Fi access point, or it is trying to join a weaker network band. Steps: 1. Look at the Wi-Fi bars on the printer display and note whether they are low. 2. Move the printer closer to a Wi-Fi access point if you can do so safely, without moving it near heat or water. 3. Turn the printer off, wait thirty seconds, and turn it back on. 4. Open the printer network settings and confirm it is connected to the staff Wi-Fi network, not the guest network. 5. Ask the help desk to check the signal strength if it still drops. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the printer location, the time it dropped, and whether it happens at the same time each day.

title: Scanned PDF is too large to send by email
body: Symptoms: You scan a document and try to email it, but the email fails or the message says the attachment is too big. Cause: The scanner saved the file at a very high resolution, which creates a large file that most email systems refuse. Steps: 1. Open the scanner settings on the printer display or the scanning app on your computer. 2. Change the resolution from high or photo quality to standard or 200 dpi for text documents. 3. Choose black and white instead of colour if you do not need colour. 4. Scan the document again and check the file size in the file details. 5. Send the email again, or split the document into two smaller files if it is still too large. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the file size shown, the number of pages, and the scanner you used.

title: Low toner warning will not clear
body: Symptoms: The printer shows a low toner message even after you have replaced the cartridge, and it may stop printing until the message is cleared. Cause: The cartridge may not be seated fully, or the printer has not recognised the new cartridge. Steps: 1. Open the front cover and take out the toner cartridge. 2. Check that the packaging tape and protective cover are fully removed from the cartridge. 3. Gently shake the cartridge side to side to spread the toner, then put it back in until it clicks. 4. Close the cover and wait for the printer to finish its startup check. 5. If the message stays, open the supplies menu and select the option to reset the cartridge count. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the printer model and the message exactly as it appears on the screen.

title: Printouts are faint or have streaks
body: Symptoms: Pages print lighter than normal, or thin lines appear across the page in the same place each time. Cause: The printer drum or print head may be dirty, or the toner is running low in one area. Steps: 1. Print a cleaning page from the printer maintenance menu, if your printer has one. 2. Remove the toner cartridge and check the drum for dust, then wipe it gently with a dry cloth. 3. Put the cartridge back in until it clicks and close the cover. 4. Print a test page and compare it with the last one. 5. Check the paper type setting matches the paper in the tray, since heavy or glossy paper can look faint. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with a photo of the streaky page and the date of the last cartridge change.

title: Scan button on the printer does nothing
body: Symptoms: You press the scan button on the printer, but the screen stays on the home page and no scan is made. Cause: The scan destination may not be set up, or the printer is waiting for a computer to be selected. Steps: 1. Look at the printer display and check whether it shows a message about a missing destination. 2. Press the back arrow and select the scan option from the main menu. 3. Choose your own name or the shared folder from the list of destinations. 4. Place the page face down on the glass or in the feeder, then press Start. 5. If no destinations appear, restart the printer and try again. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the printer location and the exact message on the screen.

title: Copies print in the wrong page order
body: Symptoms: A document with several pages prints out of order, or every copy starts with the last page. Cause: The print settings are set to print in reverse order, or the document was sent with the collate option set incorrectly. Steps: 1. Open the print window from your document before pressing Print. 2. Look for an option called Order, Reverse, or Collate and check the setting. 3. Set the page order to normal or forward, and turn collate on if you want full copies together. 4. Print one copy first to check the order. 5. Save the setting as your default if you always print this way. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the document type, the number of copies, and a description of the order you see.

title: Photos print with the wrong colours
body: Symptoms: Colour photos or graphics print too dull, too yellow, or with a strong colour tint compared with the screen. Cause: The colour profile or paper type setting does not match the paper, or the printer colour mode is set to a basic option. Steps: 1. Open the print window and choose the same paper type as the paper in the tray, such as photo paper or plain paper. 2. Set the print quality to high or best, then choose the colour option rather than greyscale. 3. Turn off any colour correction or enhancement options that your printer offers. 4. Print one test copy and compare it with the screen. 5. If the tint is still wrong, ask the help desk to check the colour cartridge levels. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the file type, the paper used, and a sample printout.

title: Phone cannot find the office printer
body: Symptoms: Your mobile phone does not show the office printer in its print list, so you cannot send a document from the phone. Cause: The phone is connected to a different Wi-Fi network from the printer, or printing from phones has not been turned on in the printer settings. Steps: 1. Check that your phone is connected to the staff Wi-Fi network, not a guest or mobile data connection. 2. Open the print option in your phone app and look for the printer list. 3. If the printer still does not appear, open the printer network settings and confirm mobile printing is switched on. 4. Restart your phone and try the print list again. 5. If it still fails, use the printer name and address from the help desk to add it manually. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with your phone model, the app you are printing from, and the printer name.

title: Scanned copies show dark lines down the page
body: Symptoms: Scanned copies have dark vertical lines running down the page, or a grey shadow appears along one edge. The printed copies from the same printer look fine. Cause: Dust, toner specks, or sticky residue has built up on the thin glass strip beside the scanner bed, or on the white strip under the lid. The scanner reads that dirt as part of the document. Steps: 1. Switch the printer off and unplug it from the wall for one minute. 2. Lift the scanner lid and find the long narrow glass strip near the edge of the scanner bed. 3. Dampen a soft lint-free cloth with plain water only, and wipe the strip gently in one direction. 4. Wipe the white strip under the lid as well. 5. Dry both surfaces with a dry cloth. Do not use cleaning sprays. 6. Plug the printer back in, wait until it is ready, then scan a blank page to check for lines. 7. If lines remain, wait a few minutes and scan the blank page again. Still stuck? If lines still appear after cleaning, scan a sample page, save a copy, and send it to the IT help desk with the printer name and your room number. Do not open the scanner casing yourself.

title: Laptop Will Not Turn On
body: Symptoms: Your laptop shows no lights, no screen image, and no fan noise when you press the power button. Cause: The battery may be fully drained, the charger may not be supplying power, or the power button may be stuck. Steps: 1. Plug the laptop into its original charger and into a wall outlet that you know works. 2. Wait ten minutes before pressing the power button again, since a fully drained battery needs time to recover. 3. Hold the power button for 15 seconds, release it, then press it once more. 4. Check whether the charging light turns on when the charger is connected. 5. Unplug any USB devices, then try again. 6. If a light appears but the screen stays black, connect an external monitor and press the power button again. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and give them the laptop asset tag, the charger model, and a description of which lights you see. Please do not open the laptop yourself.

title: Battery Drains Too Quickly
body: Symptoms: Your laptop battery falls from full to empty in only a few hours, even when you only use your email app and a web browser. The battery percentage may also jump up and down without warning. Cause: Old batteries lose capacity over time, and some apps or browser tabs keep running in the background and use power. Steps: 1. Click the battery icon in the taskbar to see which apps are using the most power. 2. Close any programs you are not using, especially video or chat apps that stay open. 3. Lower the screen brightness using the keyboard brightness keys. 4. Turn on battery saver mode from the battery icon or the settings menu. 5. Restart your laptop once a day so that background updates can finish and memory is cleared. 6. Check that Wi-Fi or Bluetooth is turned off when you are not using them. 7. Write down how many hours the battery lasts so you can compare results later. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and ask for a battery health check. If the battery is past its normal lifespan, they can arrange a replacement.

title: Laptop Overheating and Loud Fan
body: Symptoms: The laptop feels very hot on the bottom or keyboard area, the fan runs loudly all the time, and the computer may slow down or shut off unexpectedly. Cause: Air vents are blocked by dust, soft surfaces, or papers, or a demanding program is using a lot of processing power. Steps: 1. Move the laptop onto a hard, flat surface such as a desk, never a bed, sofa, or your lap. 2. Check that nothing is covering the air vents on the sides or back of the laptop. 3. Save your work and restart the laptop to stop any program that may be running too hard. 4. Open the task manager from the taskbar and look for any program using a very high percentage of the processor. Close it if you do not recognize it or do not need it. 5. Keep the laptop away from direct sunlight and heaters. 6. Do not use a cleaning spray or compressed air inside the laptop yourself. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. They can check for dust buildup or a failing fan and arrange a service visit if needed.

title: Keyboard Keys Not Responding
body: Symptoms: One or more keys on your laptop keyboard do not type, type the wrong character, or repeat by themselves. Sometimes the whole keyboard stops working after a spill. Cause: Dust or crumbs may be trapped under the keys, a key may be stuck, the keyboard setting may have changed, or a driver may need a restart. Steps: 1. Turn off the laptop and gently turn it upside down, then tap the base lightly to remove loose crumbs. 2. Use a soft cloth lightly dampened with water to wipe the keys. Never spray liquid directly on the keyboard. 3. Restart the laptop to clear any temporary keyboard errors. 4. Check whether an external keyboard works. If it does, the problem is with the laptop keyboard. 5. Open the on-screen keyboard from the accessibility settings to test whether the keys respond on screen. 6. If you spilled a drink on the laptop, turn it off right away and stop using it. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Do not try to remove keys or open the laptop base, because this can cause further damage and may affect your warranty.

title: Touchpad Not Responding
body: Symptoms: The cursor does not move when you slide your finger across the touchpad, or it moves erratically, jumps around, or clicks by itself. Cause: The touchpad may be turned off by a key combination, the setting may have changed, or a driver may need an update or restart. Steps: 1. Look at the function keys across the top of the keyboard for a key with a touchpad icon and press it together with the Fn key. 2. Open the mouse settings from the start menu and check that the touchpad is turned on. 3. Plug in a regular USB mouse to see whether the problem is only with the touchpad. 4. Restart the laptop to refresh the touchpad driver. 5. Clean the touchpad gently with a dry microfiber cloth to remove oil and dirt. 6. Make sure your hands are dry and not wet with lotion when you use it. 7. Turn off tapping if the cursor clicks when you do not intend it. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them whether the problem happens all the time or only sometimes. They can check for a driver update or a faulty part.

title: No Sound From Laptop Speakers
body: Symptoms: Videos, calls, or music play with no sound from the laptop speakers, or the sound is very quiet or crackles. Cause: The volume may be muted, the wrong playback device may be selected, headphones may still be plugged in, or the audio driver needs a restart. Steps: 1. Check the volume icon in the taskbar and make sure it is not muted and the volume is turned up. 2. Unplug any headphones or headset from the audio port on the side of the laptop. 3. Right-click the volume icon and choose sound settings. 4. Under output, select the laptop speakers as the device you want to use. 5. Play a short test sound and watch the volume bar to confirm the sound is reaching the speakers. 6. Restart the laptop to refresh the audio driver. 7. If the sound is distorted, lower the volume slightly, since very high volume can cause crackling. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and describe whether the sound is missing in all apps or only in one app. If the speakers still do not work, the hardware may need repair.

title: Docking Station Not Charging Laptop
body: Symptoms: When you place your laptop on the docking station, the laptop battery does not charge, the charging light on the laptop stays off, or the battery drains even though the dock is connected. Cause: The dock power adapter may not be plugged in, the cable connecting the dock to the laptop may be loose, or the dock may not be compatible with the laptop model. Steps: 1. Check that the power adapter for the docking station is plugged into both the dock and a working wall outlet. 2. Look for the power light on the docking station and confirm that it is lit. 3. Unplug the cable between the dock and the laptop, wait 30 seconds, then reconnect it firmly. 4. Remove the laptop from the dock and connect only the laptop charger to confirm the charger works. 5. Restart the laptop while it is connected to the dock. 6. Make sure you are using the dock connector cable that came with the dock, not a generic cable. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them the dock model, the laptop model, and whether the dock power light is on. They can check compatibility and replace the dock if needed.

title: Webcam Not Working in Video Calls
body: Symptoms: During a video call, your picture is black, frozen, or shows a message saying no camera was found. Other people may not see you at all. Cause: The camera privacy shutter may be closed, another app may already be using the camera, camera permission may be blocked, or the camera driver needs a restart. Steps: 1. Look at the top of the screen for a small sliding cover and make sure it is open. 2. Close any other video or photo app that might be using the camera. 3. Restart the laptop to free up the camera. 4. Open your chat or video app settings and choose the correct camera from the list. 5. Check the camera permission settings in the privacy section of your laptop settings and allow the app to use the camera. 6. Test the camera with the built-in camera app to see whether it works outside of your meeting app. 7. Keep the laptop screen lid open while the call is running. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them which video app you use and what message appears on screen. They can check the camera driver and settings for you.

title: USB Device Not Recognized
body: Symptoms: You plug a USB memory stick, mouse, printer cable, or other device into your laptop, but nothing happens. No icon appears in File Explorer and the device does not show up in the app you are using. Cause: The USB port may be loose or dusty, the device may be faulty, the cable may be damaged, or the laptop may need a restart to recognize new hardware. Steps: 1. Unplug the device and plug it into a different USB port on the laptop. 2. Try the same device on another computer to find out whether the device itself is working. 3. Use a different cable if the device connects with one. 4. Check the port for dust or bent pins, and remove any debris with a dry wooden toothpick or cotton swab. 5. Restart the laptop with the device connected. 6. Open the device manager from the start menu and look for a yellow warning icon next to the device name. 7. Remove the device safely before unplugging it so files are not damaged. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the device type, the port you used, and a description of any messages that appear. Do not force the device into the port.

title: Laptop Cannot Connect to Wi-Fi Hardware Switch
body:
Symptoms: Your laptop shows no Wi-Fi networks, or the Wi-Fi option is greyed out. Other people on the same floor can connect without trouble.

Cause: Many laptops have a physical wireless switch or a function key that turns Wi-Fi off. It can be switched off by accident, for example when you press a key near the top row while carrying the laptop in a bag.

Steps:
1. Look along the edges of your laptop for a small switch or indicator labelled with a wireless or antenna symbol. Slide or press it to turn Wi-Fi on.
2. Look for a function key with a wireless or airplane symbol on the top row. Hold the Fn key and press that key to toggle Wi-Fi.
3. Check that airplane mode is off in your quick settings panel.
4. Open your network settings and confirm Wi-Fi is switched on.
5. Restart your laptop and try again.

Still stuck? Note whether the Wi-Fi symbol appears in the taskbar. Contact the IT help desk and tell us the make and model shown on the bottom of your laptop so we can check the wireless adapter.

title: Laptop Screen Flickering or Shimmering
body: Symptoms: The screen flashes, shimmers, or flickers on and off, especially when you move the lid or open a document. Cause: This is usually a loose display cable, a wrong display setting, or an outdated display driver. Steps: 1. Save your work and restart your laptop. 2. Press the brightness keys once to see whether the flicker changes. 3. Close the lid gently and reopen it, making sure nothing presses on the screen edge. 4. Open the display settings, go to Advanced display, and check that the resolution and refresh rate match the recommended setting. 5. Open the software update tool and install any pending display driver updates. 6. Restart again. If the flicker only happens on an external monitor, unplug and firmly reconnect the video cable. Still stuck? Record a short video of the flicker with your phone and log a ticket with the IT service desk. Include your asset tag and whether the problem happens on battery or mains power.

title: Battery Percentage Jumps or Stays Stuck
body: Symptoms: The battery icon shows a percentage that jumps suddenly, for example from 60 percent down to 15 percent within a minute, or it stays stuck at the same number for hours. The laptop may also shut down while the screen still shows plenty of charge. Cause: The battery meter learns its capacity over time. After months of use, or after many partial charges, the meter can fall out of step with the real battery level. A worn battery can also make the reading unreliable. Steps: 1. Save your work and plug the laptop into its charger. 2. Shut the laptop down completely, wait 30 seconds, then turn it back on. 3. Unplug the charger and let the battery run down until the laptop turns off by itself. 4. Leave the laptop off for at least five hours. 5. Plug the charger back in and charge to 100 percent without using the laptop. 6. Leave it on the charger for another two hours, then unplug and check the reading. 7. If the percentage still jumps, open the battery health report from the settings menu and note the wear level. Still stuck? If the health report shows heavy wear or the laptop shuts down unexpectedly, contact the IT help desk and include the battery report. Do not open the laptop yourself, as the battery may need replacing under warranty.

title: Laptop Not Charging When Plugged In
body: Symptoms: The charger light is on, but the battery percentage stays flat or drops while the laptop is plugged in. The laptop may feel warm near the charging port. Cause: A faulty power adapter, a loose or damaged charging socket, or a battery that can no longer hold charge. Steps: 1. Check that the power cable is pushed fully into the adapter and the adapter into the wall socket. 2. Try a different wall socket that you know works. 3. Look at the charging port on your laptop for dust, bent pins, or burn marks. Do not poke it with metal objects. 4. Gently wiggle the plug while watching the charge light. If it flickers, the connection is loose. 5. Restart the laptop with the charger connected. 6. Open the battery report from the power settings to check battery health. 7. Do not use an adapter from a different laptop model. Still stuck? Stop using the charger if it feels hot or smells of burning. Report the fault to the IT service desk and bring the laptop and adapter to the support desk for inspection.

title: Keyboard Backlight Not Working
body: Symptoms: The keys do type correctly, but the backlight that lights them in dim rooms is off or will not change brightness. Cause: The backlight is switched off or turned down in settings, the backlight key combination was pressed by accident, or the keyboard light setting has stopped responding after an update. Steps: 1. Look for a keyboard key with a light or sun symbol, often on the top row. 2. Press that key once, then again, while holding the Function key if your laptop needs it. 3. Check for a keyboard backlight setting in the laptop settings under Keyboard or Input. 4. Set brightness to a level above zero and save. 5. Restart the laptop to refresh the setting. 6. Make sure the room lighting is not so bright that the backlight is hard to see. 7. Install any pending firmware or keyboard software updates. Still stuck? Tell the IT service desk your laptop model and whether the backlight ever worked. A technician can check whether the keyboard needs replacing.

title: External Monitor Shows No Picture
body: Symptoms: You connect a monitor to your laptop, but the monitor screen stays black or shows a no signal message. The laptop screen works normally. Cause: The wrong input source is selected on the monitor, the video cable is not seated properly, or the laptop display output is set to show only the laptop screen. Steps: 1. Check that the monitor is turned on and set to the correct input, such as HDMI 1 or DisplayPort. 2. Unplug the video cable at both ends and push it back in firmly. 3. Press the display switch key on your laptop, often marked with a screen symbol, and choose Extend or Duplicate. 4. Open display settings and click Detect if the monitor is not listed. 5. Try a different cable or port on your laptop, such as the one closest to the screen edge. 6. Restart the laptop with the monitor already connected. 7. If you use a docking station, connect the monitor directly to the laptop to test. Still stuck? Tell the IT service desk which cable and port you used and the monitor model. A technician can test whether the monitor or the laptop port is faulty.

title: Microphone Not Picking Up Your Voice
body: Symptoms: Colleagues say they cannot hear you on calls, or the microphone level bar does not move when you speak. Cause: The wrong microphone is selected, the microphone is muted in the app or the system, or the app does not have permission to use the microphone. Steps: 1. Look at the microphone icon in the call app and make sure it is not crossed out. 2. Check the mute key on your keyboard, if your laptop has one. 3. Open sound settings and find the Input section. 4. Choose the built-in microphone or your headset from the list, then speak and watch the level bar. 5. Raise the input volume if the bar moves only slightly. 6. Open privacy settings and confirm that the call app is allowed to use the microphone. 7. Close the call app fully and reopen it. Still stuck? Test your microphone in a voice recording app. If the recording is silent, report the problem to the IT service desk so they can check the hardware.

title: Laptop Shuts Down Without Warning
body: Symptoms: The laptop switches off suddenly during normal work, sometimes with no warning, and the screen goes black. It may take a few minutes before it can be turned on again. Cause: The battery is worn or not reporting its level correctly, the laptop is overheating and protects itself, or a recent update has caused a fault. Steps: 1. Check whether the shutdowns happen on battery power only or also when plugged in. 2. Make sure the air vents on the sides and bottom are not blocked by paper or a cushion. 3. Use the laptop on a hard, flat surface. 4. Save your work often until the problem is solved. 5. Open the battery report from the power settings to check battery health. 6. Install any pending system updates and restart. 7. Turn off any heavy programs that you do not need. Still stuck? Write down the approximate time of each shutdown and what you were doing. Send this to the IT service desk, as it helps them check the system logs.

title: Bluetooth Mouse Will Not Pair
body: Symptoms: Your wireless mouse does not appear in the list of Bluetooth devices, or it pairs once and then stops working. The mouse light may blink without connecting. Cause: The mouse is not in pairing mode, its battery is low, or Bluetooth is turned off or still linked to an older device. Steps: 1. Replace or recharge the mouse batteries. 2. Turn the mouse off and on again. 3. Hold the pairing button on the mouse until the light blinks quickly. 4. Open Bluetooth settings on your laptop and make sure Bluetooth is turned on. 5. Remove any old entry for the mouse in the device list. 6. Choose Add device and select the mouse when it appears. 7. Keep the mouse within one metre of the laptop during pairing. Still stuck? If the mouse still does not connect, try a USB receiver if the mouse came with one. Otherwise, contact the IT service desk to request a replacement mouse.

title: SD Card Reader Not Reading Cards
body: Symptoms: You insert an SD card into the laptop slot, but nothing appears in File Explorer, or the laptop asks you to format the card. Cause: The card is not pushed in fully, the card is dirty or damaged, the reader needs a driver, or the card is locked. Steps: 1. Turn the card so the label faces up and gently push it in until it clicks. 2. Remove the card and check the gold contacts for dust. Wipe them with a dry cloth. 3. Check the small lock switch on the side of the card and set it to the unlocked position. 4. Try the card in a different slot or on another computer to see whether the card or the reader is faulty. 5. Open Device Manager and check for a warning on the card reader. Update the driver if you see one. 6. Restart the laptop with the card inserted. Do not click Format if the card contains work files. Still stuck? Contact the IT service desk and say whether the card works elsewhere. Do not reuse a card that shows physical damage.

title: Screen Too Dark Even at Full Brightness
body: Symptoms: The screen is dim or hard to read even when the brightness is set to maximum. Colours may look washed out, but the picture is still visible. Cause: The brightness setting is limited by a power or battery saving mode, an automatic brightness feature is adjusting the level, or the display backlight is wearing out. Steps: 1. Press the brightness up key several times and watch the on-screen brightness bar. 2. Open display settings and turn off any automatic brightness option. 3. Check the battery or power settings and turn off battery saver mode, which can cap brightness. 4. Turn off any night light or colour comfort setting that reduces brightness. 5. Restart the laptop and check again. 6. Connect the laptop to mains power and see whether brightness returns to normal. 7. Shine a torch sideways at the screen in a dark room to see if the picture is still there. Still stuck? Report the issue to the IT service desk. If the screen is dim only on one side, the backlight may need repair.

title: Laptop cannot find the office Wi-Fi
body: Symptoms: Your laptop does not list the office Wi-Fi network when you open the Wi-Fi menu, or it only shows networks from nearby homes and shops. Colleagues sitting near you may still connect without any trouble. Cause: Wi-Fi may be switched off on the laptop, airplane mode may be turned on, or the wireless adapter may be stuck and need a restart. Steps: 1. Click the Wi-Fi icon in the taskbar and confirm that Wi-Fi is switched on. 2. Turn off airplane mode if it is active. 3. Select Refresh in the Wi-Fi list, or move closer to the nearest wall-mounted access point in your area. 4. Restart your laptop, wait for it to finish starting up, and check the list again. 5. If the office network still does not appear, ask the service desk whether the network name has recently changed. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them your laptop model, your building and floor, and whether a colleague nearby can see the network.

title: Connected to Wi-Fi but no internet
body: Symptoms: The Wi-Fi icon shows that you are connected, yet web pages will not load, your email app shows an offline message, and the chat app stays grey. Other systems that use a cable may still work. Cause: Your laptop has joined the network, but the connection to the wider internet is interrupted, or your laptop has taken an outdated network address. Steps: 1. Open a web browser and try to load one internal site, then one public site, so you know whether the problem affects everything. 2. Turn Wi-Fi off for ten seconds, then turn it back on and wait for the connection to settle. 3. Restart your laptop, since this refreshes its network address. 4. Make sure the company VPN app is not stuck in a half-connected state; disconnect it if it is open. 5. If none of this helps, write down the exact time the problem started and the name of the Wi-Fi network you joined. Still stuck? Send these details to the IT help desk. If the problem affects many people in your office at once, tell them so, because this usually means a wider outage that they need to investigate.

title: Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting
body: Symptoms: Your laptop drops off the office Wi-Fi every few minutes, video calls freeze, and files stop uploading before they finish. The Wi-Fi icon may flicker or briefly show no connection. Cause: The most common causes are a weak signal from a distant access point, an outdated wireless driver, or power-saving settings that switch the wireless adapter off to save battery. Steps: 1. Move closer to a wall-mounted access point or a window if you are working far from one. 2. Plug your laptop into its charger, because some laptops reduce Wi-Fi power when running on battery. 3. Open the power settings for your wireless adapter in Device Manager and clear the option that allows the computer to turn it off. 4. Restart your laptop after making the change. 5. Note the times when disconnections happen and whether they coincide with busy periods such as lunch or large meetings. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with your laptop model, your location, and the approximate times the drops occur. They can check the access points that cover your area and update your wireless driver if needed.

title: Wi-Fi is very slow
body: Symptoms: Web pages take a long time to load, files download slowly, and video calls become blurry or stop and start. Speed tests may show much lower numbers than usual. Cause: Slow Wi-Fi is often caused by too many devices on one access point, background downloads or updates on your laptop, a weak signal, or a fault in a single access point. Steps: 1. Close large downloads, cloud backups, and video streams that you do not need. 2. Pause any operating system updates that are running in the background. 3. Move closer to the nearest access point, or sit in the same room as a colleague who has a faster connection. 4. Restart your laptop to clear stuck processes and reconnect to the network. 5. Run a speed test in your browser and note the result, along with the time and your location. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and send them your speed test results and location. If the slowness happens only in one room, they can check that access point. If it happens across the building, the issue may be shared network traffic that the team needs to manage.

title: Wrong password error when joining office Wi-Fi
body: Symptoms: When you select the office Wi-Fi network, a box appears asking for a password, and it keeps rejecting what you type, even though you are sure it is correct. Your laptop may say the security settings are incorrect. Cause: The Wi-Fi password was recently changed, your laptop is storing an old saved password, or the password has been mistyped because of capital letters or similar-looking characters. Steps: 1. Open the Wi-Fi settings on your laptop and choose the option to forget the office network. 2. Select the network again and type the current password slowly, checking capital letters and symbols. 3. Turn off caps lock and try typing the password into a notepad first to check it. 4. If you use a phone that is already on the network, do not reuse its saved password, because it may be out of date. 5. Restart your laptop after joining the network successfully. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and confirm you are using the staff network and not the guest network. Do not share the password with anyone else. The help desk can confirm the current password and reset your access if required.

title: Guest Wi-Fi sign-in page does not appear
body: Symptoms: You connect to the guest Wi-Fi network for a visitor or for a personal device, but no sign-in page opens. Instead, the browser shows an error or keeps loading a page that never appears. Cause: The sign-in page is sometimes blocked when a browser tries to open a secure website first, or when the device has old security settings. The connection may also still be waiting for approval. Steps: 1. Open a new browser tab and type a simple address such as the company main site, which often triggers the sign-in page. 2. If nothing appears, close all browser windows and try again in a private or incognito window. 3. Turn off any browser extensions that block pop-ups or advertisements, then reload the page. 4. Forget the guest network on the device, reconnect, and wait about thirty seconds before opening a page. 5. Try a different device to confirm whether the problem is with the device or the network. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Give them the name of the guest network, the device type, and the exact message shown on screen. Visitors should not be asked to enter staff passwords.

title: Phone will not join office Wi-Fi after a change
body: Symptoms: Your phone was working on the office Wi-Fi yesterday, but today it keeps saying it cannot connect, or it shows a permanent spinning icon while it tries to join. Other devices may still connect without trouble. Cause: Phones save old network details. After a password or security change, the saved information no longer matches the network, so the phone keeps trying the wrong details. Steps: 1. Open the Wi-Fi settings on your phone and select the office network. 2. Choose the option to forget or remove the network from saved networks. 3. Turn Wi-Fi off, wait ten seconds, and turn it back on. 4. Select the office network again and type the current password carefully. 5. Restart the phone if it still fails, then check that the chat app and email app are working. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them your phone model and whether the problem started after a recent password change. Do not keep retrying many times in a row, because some networks temporarily block devices that try too often. The help desk can confirm whether your phone is allowed on the staff network.

title: Video calls drop in the meeting room
body: Symptoms: Video calls work well at your desk but freeze, pixelate, or disconnect when you join a call in a meeting room. Audio may cut out in the middle of sentences, and screen sharing may stop without warning. Cause: Meeting rooms are often far from access points, or thick walls and glass can weaken the signal. Many people using the room at the same time can also slow the connection. Steps: 1. Before the meeting, check the Wi-Fi bars on your laptop in the meeting room, rather than waiting until the call starts. 2. If the signal is weak, ask the room booking team whether a nearer desk or room is available. 3. Use the cable in the meeting room if one is provided, since a wired connection is more stable. 4. Close other apps that use bandwidth, such as file sync tools and streaming windows. 5. Report the room number and the time of the problem to the IT help desk so they can check it. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the room name, the date and time, and what happened during the call. They can review the signal strength in that room and arrange a fix or a better location for future meetings.

title: Company VPN app will not connect over Wi-Fi
body: Symptoms: Your laptop is connected to Wi-Fi and the internet works, but the company VPN app stays on Connecting or shows an error message. Internal websites and shared drives do not open while the VPN app is trying to connect. Cause: Some home or hotel networks block the connection the VPN app needs, or the VPN app is out of date, or the laptop's date and time settings are wrong. Steps: 1. Confirm your laptop shows the correct date and time, and turn on automatic time setting if it is off. 2. Restart the VPN app and then try to connect again. 3. If you are on a public or hotel network, try a different Wi-Fi network, such as your mobile hotspot, for a short test. 4. Check that the VPN app is up to date by using the update option in its menu. 5. Restart your laptop if the connection still fails, and then try once more. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and copy the exact error message shown by the VPN app. Include the Wi-Fi network you used, such as home or hotel, and whether it worked before. Do not turn off security features to force the connection.

title: Docking station gives no network connection
body: Symptoms: Your laptop is plugged into the docking station at your desk, but it shows no wired network connection. Your screen may work, but the network icon shows a warning, and shared drives or internal websites do not open. Cause: The network cable may not be seated properly in the dock, the dock may need a firmware or driver update, or the laptop may still be using the Wi-Fi connection without the wired one. Steps: 1. Unplug the laptop from the dock, wait ten seconds, then plug it back in firmly. 2. Check that the network cable is fully clicked into both the dock and the wall socket. 3. Restart your laptop while it is connected to the dock. 4. Open the network settings and confirm that the wired connection is listed and turned on. 5. Try a different cable or a different port on the dock if you have one available. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them your desk number, the dock model, and whether the screen works through the dock. A faulty dock or wall socket can be replaced quickly once the help desk has confirmed the cause.

title: Office Wi-Fi name missing from the phone list
body: Symptoms: Your phone's Wi-Fi list shows neighbouring networks and guest networks, but the office Wi-Fi name does not appear, even when you are in the office. Colleagues nearby may see it without trouble. Cause: The phone may have Wi-Fi switched off for a moment, be in airplane mode, or have an old saved network that hides the office name after an update. Steps: 1) Turn off airplane mode and make sure Wi-Fi is switched on. 2) Pull down on the Wi-Fi list to refresh it and wait ten seconds. 3) Move closer to a window or a wall-mounted access point and check again. 4) Open Settings, go to Wi-Fi, and forget any saved office network with the same name. 5) Restart the phone, then reconnect by choosing the office network and entering your normal staff login. 6) Check that the phone is not in a low-power mode that limits Wi-Fi scanning. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them your phone model, the room you are in, and whether a colleague's phone nearby can see the network. Never share your password by text or email.

title: Wi-Fi connects but drops after laptop wakes from sleep
body: Symptoms: When you open your laptop after leaving it closed or idle, the Wi-Fi icon shows connected, but web pages and the chat app will not load for a minute or two. Sometimes the connection drops again after a few minutes of use. Cause: Laptops can switch off the Wi-Fi adapter to save power when they sleep. When it wakes, the adapter may not rejoin the network cleanly, especially if the power plan is set to save energy aggressively. Steps: 1) Click the Wi-Fi icon and turn Wi-Fi off, wait five seconds, then turn it back on. 2) Open Settings, choose Network, and confirm you are on the office network. 3) Open Device Manager, find the Wi-Fi adapter under Network adapters, open its Properties, and on the Power Management tab untick the option that allows the computer to turn it off. 4) Restart the laptop once to apply the change. 5) Test by closing the lid for five minutes, then reopening it and loading a web page. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and say how long the laptop was asleep before the problem started. Do not change other network settings without guidance, as this can cause new problems.

title: Password accepted but device asks again each morning
body: Symptoms: You type the office Wi-Fi password correctly and connect, but the next morning your laptop or phone asks for the password again. Sometimes the prompt appears after a restart or once a week. Cause: The saved network profile on the device may be corrupted, or the device is storing an old password after a recent password change. Some devices also forget networks when they have not seen them for a while. Steps: 1) Click the Wi-Fi icon, select the office network, and choose Forget or Remove. 2) Restart the device to clear any stuck connection data. 3) Reconnect to the office network and enter your current staff password exactly as written in your staff portal. 4) Tick the option to connect automatically, if your device offers it. 5) Check that the device date and time are correct, since wrong times can break saved logins. 6) Leave the device on the office network for a few minutes so it can refresh its settings. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them the device type, when the prompt started, and whether you changed your password recently. Never write your password on a sticky note near the device.

title: Printer cannot be found on the office network
body: Symptoms: Your computer's print list does not show the floor printer, or it shows the printer but sending a job gives an error saying the printer is offline. Colleagues on the same floor may be printing without trouble. Cause: The computer may be connected to a different network than the printer, such as the guest Wi-Fi, or its printer setup may point to an old address that was removed. Steps: 1) Check the Wi-Fi name in the corner of your screen and confirm it is the office network, not guest access. 2) Open Printers and Scanners in Settings and look for the printer name on your floor. 3) If it is missing, select Add a printer and let the computer search for devices nearby. 4) If it appears but shows offline, remove it, restart the computer, and add it again. 5) Print a single test page to confirm the connection works. 6) Make sure the printer has paper, its display shows ready, and no error light is flashing. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and give them the printer name shown on the label, your floor, and the exact error message. Do not install drivers from websites you find yourself.

title: Shared drive will not open over Wi-Fi
body: Symptoms: The shared drive folder shows an error saying the network path cannot be found, or it opens very slowly and then times out. Local files on your laptop still open normally. Cause: The laptop may be on a Wi-Fi network that is not allowed to reach the file servers, or it may have lost its connection to the drive while switching between access points. Steps: 1) Confirm you are on the office network, not the guest network or a personal hotspot. 2) Close the folder window and open it again from the Files app using the drive name your team normally uses. 3) If it asks for your login, enter your normal staff username and password. 4) Restart the Wi-Fi by turning it off and on, then try again. 5) If you are in a meeting room or at the far end of the floor, move closer to a desk and retry. 6) Save your open work to your laptop so nothing is lost while the connection is fixed. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them which drive or folder you were trying to reach, the exact error message, and roughly where you were in the building. Do not copy shared files to unknown USB sticks.

title: Video calls fine at desk but freeze in the open area
body: Symptoms: On a video call at your desk, the picture and sound are clear. When you move to the open seating area or a corner of the floor, the video freezes, the sound breaks up, and the call reconnects after a while. Cause: The Wi-Fi signal may be weaker in that area, or the device may be switching between access points and losing packets during the handover. Steps: 1) Note where the problem happens and check the Wi-Fi bars on your device while you are there. 2) Turn off the camera for that call to see if audio stays steady, which tells you whether the signal is weak. 3) Move closer to the nearest window or access point, or sit at a desk you know works well. 4) Close other heavy apps, such as large downloads or cloud backups, that share your connection. 5) If possible, plug your laptop into a wired desk connection for important calls. 6) Report the spot to the IT help desk so the signal can be checked. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the room or desk number, the time of day, and the name of the call app you were using. Do not restart the call repeatedly, as this can cause extra disconnections.

title: Security warning about the Wi-Fi certificate
body: Symptoms: When you join the office Wi-Fi or open the chat app, a pop-up appears saying the security certificate is untrusted, expired, or does not match the network name. You may be asked whether to continue. Cause: The device may not have the latest company security certificate, or the network may be showing a fake network with the same name nearby. Steps: 1) Do not click Continue or Trust yet. 2) Cancel the pop-up and check the Wi-Fi name carefully, including spelling and spacing. 3) Look at the list of nearby networks to see whether there are two networks with the same name. 4) If the name is correct and only one appears, forget the network on your device and reconnect using your staff login. 5) Make sure the device date and time are correct, since a wrong clock can make a valid certificate look expired. 6) Take a photo of the warning and note the time you saw it. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk right away, send them the photo, and say where you were when the warning appeared. Never accept a certificate warning if you are unsure, as it may mean someone is trying to capture your password.

title: Phone hotspot will not share to laptop
body: Symptoms: You turn on your phone's hotspot to work from a location without office Wi-Fi, but your laptop cannot see the hotspot name, or it connects and then says there is no internet. Cause: The hotspot may be turned off by a power saving setting, the phone may be set to only share on mobile data that is currently unavailable, or the laptop may have a saved profile for a different hotspot. Steps: 1) On your phone, open Settings and go to Hotspot and tethering, then confirm Mobile hotspot is switched on. 2) Check that your phone has mobile data or a signal, since the hotspot cannot share a connection you do not have. 3) Note the hotspot name and password shown on the phone. 4) On your laptop, forget any old network with the same name, then choose the hotspot and enter the password exactly. 5) Keep the phone close to the laptop and the screen unlocked while connecting. 6) Turn the hotspot off and on again if the laptop still does not connect. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them your phone model, your laptop model, and whether the hotspot name appears at all. Do not use hotspots in public places to open staff systems unless your manager has approved it.

title: Remote desktop disconnects on a home connection
body: Symptoms: When you connect to your office computer from home, the remote session works for a few minutes, then freezes and shows a message saying the connection was lost. Reconnecting may work briefly before dropping again. Cause: Home Wi-Fi may be overloaded by other devices, the router may be weak in your room, or the remote desktop app may be using a setting that does not suit a home connection. Steps: 1) Before connecting, close streaming videos, large downloads, and cloud backups on your home network. 2) Move your laptop closer to the router or connect it to the router with a cable if you can. 3) Restart your home router by unplugging it for thirty seconds, then plugging it back in and waiting five minutes. 4) Open the remote desktop app and lower the display quality setting to reduce the data being sent. 5) Reconnect and note whether the session stays stable for longer. 6) Keep your office computer switched on and unlocked as usual, and do not put it to sleep during remote work. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the time of the disconnects and your approximate distance from the router. Do not turn off the router permanently or change its security settings without help.

title: Wi-Fi network name appears twice in the list
body: Symptoms: When you open the Wi-Fi list, the office network name appears two times, or appears with small differences such as an extra space or a different ending. Connecting to one version sometimes fails. Cause: The office may use more than one access point type, or an older network profile may still be saved on your device with a slightly different name. Steps: 1) Write down exactly how each name looks, including spaces and capital letters. 2) Look for the staff name listed by the IT team in your welcome email or staff portal. 3) Forget any saved network that does not match the approved staff name. 4) Choose the approved name, enter your normal staff login, and connect. 5) Confirm the connection by opening a web page that you normally use at work. 6) If both names are on the approved list, connect to the one that gives you the best signal at your desk. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and send them a photo of the Wi-Fi list, with your personal details hidden, along with the name of your building and floor. Do not connect to any network that you do not recognise, even if it has a similar name.

title: VPN app will not connect
body: Symptoms: The company VPN app shows Connecting and then fails, or reports that the server cannot be reached. You may see a timed out message while working from home or on a hotel network. Cause: The VPN app usually fails when your internet connection is unstable, when a local firewall blocks it, or when an old version of the app is installed. Steps: 1. Confirm your internet works by opening any website in your browser. 2. Restart your laptop, then open the VPN app again. 3. Open the app's Help menu and choose Check for updates, then install any update offered. 4. Turn off any other VPN or security add-on you installed yourself. 5. Try connecting from a different network, such as a phone hotspot. 6. Sign out of the VPN app, sign back in, and try again. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and include the exact error message, the network you are on, and the time you tried. Never share your password in the message.

title: Cannot install approved software
body: Symptoms: When you open an installer, a message says you need administrator approval, or the install stops with an access denied error. Cause: Company laptops are set so that only IT can add new programs. This protects the company from harmful software. Steps: 1. Open the software portal app on your laptop instead of running the installer file directly. 2. Search for the program by name. 3. If it is listed as approved, select Install and wait for it to finish. 4. If the button is grey or the program is missing, select Request software and write the business reason. 5. Do not try to turn off security tools or change system settings to get around the block. 6. Watch your email for the approval message, which usually takes one business day. 7. After approval, open the portal again, select Install, and restart if asked. Still stuck? Reply to your request ticket with the program name, the version you need, and your manager's name so IT can speed up the review.

title: Locked out after password change
body: Symptoms: After changing your work password, your email app, chat app, or other tools keep asking for a password, or they say your account is locked. Cause: Apps save the old password on your laptop or phone. When the password changes, those saved copies no longer work, and too many failed tries can lock the account for a short time. Steps: 1. Wait five minutes so the account can unlock automatically if it was locked. 2. Close every work app on your laptop and phone. 3. Sign in to the company login page in your browser using your new password. 4. Open your email app and enter the new password when prompted. 5. Repeat for the chat app and any other work tools, one at a time. 6. On your phone, remove old work accounts from the settings and add them again. 7. Restart your laptop once everything works. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Do not keep trying the old password, because repeated failures can lock the account for longer.

title: Authenticator code is rejected
body: Symptoms: When you sign in, the login page asks for a six digit code from the authenticator app, but the code is marked as invalid or expired. Cause: The codes change every thirty seconds. If the clock on your phone is wrong or you type an old code, the login fails. Steps: 1. Open the authenticator app on your phone and look at the code for the company account. 2. Type the newest code right away, before it changes. 3. If it still fails, check your phone settings and turn on automatic date and time. 4. Restart your phone, then open the authenticator app again. 5. Make sure you are using the account labeled with the company name, not a personal one. 6. Wait for a fresh code to appear, then try once more. 7. Do not try many codes in a row, because the login may lock for a short time. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and say whether you have changed phones recently. They can reset your authenticator setup after checking your identity.

title: App missing from software portal
body: Symptoms: You open the software portal and cannot find an app that a coworker in another team uses. The portal may show only a few programs, or the app is labeled not available. Cause: Software is assigned by job role and department. Your role may not include that app, or the license for it may be fully used. Steps: 1. Open the software portal and select the search box. 2. Type the program name and check the spelling, including any version number. 3. Look at the Requirements or Details section of the app for who can use it. 4. If your role should have access, select Request software and mention your job title and team. 5. If the app is needed for a specific project, include the project name in your request. 6. Do not download the program from a website or share a login with a coworker. 7. Check your ticket status in the portal each day. Still stuck? Contact your manager to confirm the app is needed for your work, then reply to your ticket with their approval so IT can act quickly.

title: Installation fails: not enough disk space
body: Symptoms: An install stops partway and shows a message about not enough space, or it says the installation could not be completed. Your laptop may also feel slow when you open files. Cause: Laptops have limited storage, and old downloads, large files, and cached data can fill it up. Most installers need several gigabytes of free space. Steps: 1. Open the Storage settings on your laptop to see how much space is free. 2. Empty your Downloads folder by moving files you no longer need to a backup location. 3. Empty the Recycle Bin or Trash. 4. Open your email app and remove large attachments you have already saved. 5. Restart your laptop to clear temporary files. 6. Try the installation again from the software portal. 7. If it still fails, note how much space is free and when the error appears. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk. Do not delete system or program folders, because that can damage your laptop. IT can check whether your laptop needs a storage upgrade.

title: Access denied to shared folder
body: Symptoms: When you open a shared network folder, a message says access denied or you do not have permission. Other people on your team can open the same folder. Cause: Shared folders are limited to specific groups. Your account may not be in the group for that folder, or you may have moved teams recently and your access has not been updated. Steps: 1. Check the folder name and location to make sure it is the one you need. 2. Ask a team member who can open it to confirm the exact folder path. 3. Sign out of your laptop, then sign back in to refresh your group membership. 4. Try opening the folder again. 5. If it still fails, submit an access request in the software portal or help desk form. 6. Include the full folder path, the reason you need access, and your manager's approval. 7. Do not copy the files to a personal storage service as a workaround. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and say when your team changed. IT can confirm your group membership and add you if approved.

title: Email app keeps asking for password
body: Symptoms: Your email app repeatedly asks for your password, even after you type it correctly. Sometimes it shows a message saying the connection to the server failed or that the sign in could not be verified. Cause: The saved login in the email app can become outdated after a password change, a security update, or a change in network. Steps: 1. Confirm that you can sign in to the company login page in your browser with your current password. 2. Close your email app completely, including any background copy. 3. Open the email app again and enter your password when prompted. 4. If the prompt returns, open the account settings and remove the company account. 5. Add the account again using your full work email address and current password. 6. If you use a phone, do the same there, then wait a few minutes for mail to sync. 7. Avoid entering the password many times in a row, because the account can lock. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and mention the device and app you use. Include any error message exactly as shown.

title: Chat app will not sign in after update
body: Symptoms: After the chat app updated itself, it opens to a blank screen, a sign in loop, or a message saying your version is no longer supported. Cause: Updates sometimes change how the app stores login details. A damaged saved session or an outdated install can stop the app from signing you in. Steps: 1. Close the chat app completely using the Quit option, not just the window close button. 2. Restart your laptop. 3. Open the software portal and check for a newer version of the chat app. 4. Install the update if one is available, then restart the app. 5. If the sign in loop continues, sign out inside the app if you can reach the menu, then sign in again. 6. If you cannot sign out, use the chat app help page to reset your session, following the on screen steps. 7. Do not reinstall from an outside website. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them your app version, which laptop you use, and when the problem started.

title: Design tool says license expired
body: Symptoms: When you open the design tool, a message says your license has expired, or the tool switches to read only mode and will not let you save or export your work. Cause: Paid software licenses are issued for set periods, and they must be renewed. Renewal can also be blocked if the license is assigned to a different person or the team has used all of its seats. Steps: 1. Note the exact message and the name of the license shown on screen. 2. Save any open work to a file in your team folder so nothing is lost. 3. Sign out of the design tool and sign back in with your work account. 4. Restart your laptop and open the tool again. 5. Open the software portal and look for the design tool under My Software. 6. If it shows expired, select Request renewal and give your manager's name. 7. Do not use a personal trial or a shared login. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and include the license name, your manager's approval, and the deadline for your project.

title: VPN app keeps disconnecting
body: Symptoms: The company VPN app connects successfully, but after a few minutes it drops off by itself. A message may say the connection was lost, and web pages or shared drives stop loading until you reconnect. This can happen several times in one hour. Cause: The connection is usually interrupted by unstable Wi-Fi, a laptop that goes to sleep, or a network setting that ends idle sessions too quickly. Steps: 1. Connect your laptop to power and turn off battery saver mode. 2. Move closer to your Wi-Fi router, or plug in a network cable if your desk has one. 3. Open the VPN app, choose Disconnect, then Connect again. 4. In your laptop settings, set sleep to Never while plugged in. 5. Restart your laptop and reconnect once more. Still stuck? If the VPN app still drops within 15 minutes, take a screenshot of the error and note the time it happened. Send both to the IT help desk and say whether you are on home Wi-Fi, office Wi-Fi, or mobile hotspot.

title: Authenticator app codes are out of sync
body: Symptoms: The six-digit code shown in the authenticator app is rejected at sign-in, even though you typed it quickly and carefully. Codes may work on one device but not another. Cause: Authenticator codes change every 30 seconds and depend on the clock on your phone being correct. If your phone clock has drifted, the codes it generates will not match the company system. Steps: 1. Open your phone settings and check that date and time are set to automatic. 2. Turn automatic time zone on as well, then restart your phone. 3. Open the authenticator app and look for a sync or time correction option, and run it if available. 4. Wait for a fresh code to appear, then sign in using only that new code. 5. If the code is still rejected, do not try many codes in a row, because the system may lock your account for a short time. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk and tell them the time shown on your phone, the time on a computer clock, and whether you recently changed phones.

title: Shared folder opens but files are read-only
body: Symptoms: You can open a shared team folder and see its files, but when you try to edit, save, rename, or delete something, you get a message that the folder is read-only or that you do not have permission to change it. Cause: Your access level may be set to view only. This often happens after a team change, or when a folder owner grants read access but not edit access. Steps: 1. Note the exact folder name and the path shown in the address bar. 2. Check with your manager whether you need edit rights for this folder or only view rights. 3. If you need edit rights, submit an access request through the IT request form and name the folder, the level you need, and your manager. 4. Wait for your manager to approve the request, since most folder changes need sign-off. 5. Once you receive confirmation, sign out of your laptop and sign back in, then try saving a test file. Still stuck? Reply to the request ticket with a screenshot of the error message. If you cannot save a file you created today, mention it, because your work may need to be moved to a folder you can edit.

title: Software portal install button is greyed out
body: Symptoms: You open the software portal, find an approved app, and the install button is greyed out or says Unavailable. Other apps on the same page may work normally. Cause: The button is disabled when the app is only available for certain departments, when your laptop does not meet the minimum system requirements, or when a previous install attempt is still waiting in the queue. Steps: 1. Click the app name and read the line that says Requirements or Availability. 2. If it names a department or role you do not belong to, stop here and ask your manager whether you need it. 3. If it lists a system requirement, such as a newer operating system version, install pending updates from your laptop settings and restart. 4. Open the software portal, select the Downloads or Queue tab, and cancel any stuck entry for the same app. 5. Close the portal completely, reopen it, and check the install button again. Still stuck? Send the IT help desk the app name, the text shown under the greyed-out button, and your laptop model, so they can confirm eligibility and clear the queue.

title: Installer closes with no message
body: Symptoms: You start an approved installer, a progress window appears briefly, and then it disappears without finishing. There is no error message, or only a short flash of text. The app does not appear in your Start menu or Applications folder. Cause: Installers often close quietly when another copy of the same app is still running in the background, when security software blocks the file, or when the download was incomplete. Steps: 1. Save any open work and restart your laptop to clear background programs. 2. Open your task manager or activity monitor and close any leftover copies of the app. 3. Delete the installer file from your Downloads folder, then download it again from the software portal. 4. Right-click the new installer and choose Run as administrator, or ask the help desk to confirm you have permission. 5. Watch the whole install, and wait until it shows a finish message before closing anything. Still stuck? Send the help desk the file name of the installer and the time you tried. If your security software blocked the file, a notice may appear in its alert history, and the help desk can review it.

title: Software request stuck waiting for approval
body: Symptoms: You submitted a request for a new work app several days ago, and the request still shows Pending or Waiting for approval. You have not received a decision or any reply. Cause: Requests move through a manager approval step, then a security review for some apps. A request can stall if the approver is away, if the wrong manager was selected, or if the request was missing a business reason. Steps: 1. Open the software request page and find your request by its reference number. 2. Read the status history to see which step it is waiting at. 3. Check that the approver named is your current manager, not a former one. 4. Send your manager a short message with the reference number and ask them to review it this week. 5. If your manager confirms the request is correct but it still has not moved after three working days, reply on the same ticket and ask for a security review date. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with the reference number and the name of the app. Do not submit a duplicate request, because that can slow down both copies.

title: Remote desktop cannot find your office computer
body: Symptoms: When you open the remote desktop app from home to reach your office computer, the name of the computer does not appear in the list, or you get a message saying the computer is offline or cannot be found. Cause: The office computer may be turned off, asleep, or not connected to the office network. Remote access also depends on the computer being set to allow connections, and the name or saved address may have changed. Steps: 1. Confirm that someone in the office can see the computer is powered on and not in sleep mode. 2. Ask a colleague to restart it if it has been on for more than a week. 3. On your home laptop, open the remote desktop app and remove the old saved entry. 4. Search the company computer list for your office computer name and add it again. 5. Try connecting, and if it asks for a code, enter it from your authenticator app. Still stuck? Contact the IT help desk with your office computer name, your home location, and the exact message shown. Do not leave the office computer running unattended overnight without asking first.

title: VPN app connects but internal sites will not load
body: Symptoms: The VPN app shows Connected with a green icon, but internal websites, shared drives and the company intranet do not open. Public websites still load normally. Cause: The connection is up, but your laptop is not receiving the internal address settings. This often happens when an older connection profile is still saved in the VPN app or when your laptop is using a different network adapter. Steps: 1. Click the VPN app icon and choose Disconnect. 2. Open the VPN app settings and remove any profile labelled Old or Legacy. 3. Restart your laptop. 4. Open the VPN app, select the current profile, and click Connect. 5.
